name: align_event_log
docs: Align an event log against a given process model and return the per-variant alignments,
aggregate fitness, and the net itself (echoed for the visualizations).

args.title: AcceptingPetriNet
args.description:
A [`PetriNet`] with an initial and a final marking

In JSON, the net's fields sit next to `initial_marking` and `final_marking`.

initial_marking.description: The marking the net starts in

final_marking.description: The marking a complete run ends in

name.description: External identifier (e.g., the PNML id), not used for identity

label.description: Activity label (`None` if this transition is silent)

name.description: External identifier (e.g., the PNML id), not used for identity

outputs.description: The places this transition puts tokens into, with the number of tokens

name: apply_event_log_transforms
docs: Apply a pipeline of transforms to an event log, returning the transformed log.

oneOf.description:
Filter traces by their exact activity sequence (variant); a trace matches if its
sequence equals any of the given variants.
Sample randomly.

amount.description: How much to sample: a fixed count or a percentage of the total.

seed.description: Random seed for reproducibility. If None, uses a default seed.

target.description: What to sample: traces (XES), objects, or events.

oneOf.description:
Keep or remove events whose timestamp falls inside the given half-open range
`[start, end)`. Traces/objects left empty by the filter are dropped too.

start.description: Inclusive start of the range (ISO 8601 / RFC 3339, e.g. "2025-01-01T00:00:00+00:00").

end.description: Exclusive end of the range (ISO 8601 / RFC 3339).

oneOf.description:
Rescale all timestamps to fit within a target timeframe.
Preserves relative ordering and proportional gaps between events.

target_start.description: Target start time (ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 string, e.g. "2025-01-01T00:00:00+00:00")

min_gap_ms.description: If set, enforce a minimum gap (in milliseconds) between consecutive events after rescaling.

max_gap_ms.description: If set, enforce a maximum gap (in milliseconds) between consecutive events after rescaling.

gap_object_type.description: For OCEL only: which object type to scope the gap clamping to.

oneOf.description: Filter events or cases/objects by attribute conditions.
Remove named attribute keys from entities in a given scope.

Match on the entity's event timestamps relative to the half-open window
`[start, end)`. Composes with the other conditions via `And`/`Or`/`Not`.
True if the entity carries the attribute `key` at all (any value).
True if the entity's own type matches: event activity, or object type.

True if the entity's `[first event, last event]` span duration (ms) is within
`[min_ms, max_ms]` (either bound optional). Atomic events have zero-length spans.

(OCEL object / XES case scope) Evaluate the sub-condition against the entity's related
events (their activity, attributes, timestamp) with the given quantifier.

Evaluate the sub-condition against related objects: at event scope over E2O-linked
objects ("events with a matching object"), at object scope over O2O-linked objects.

TimeframeMode.description:
How an entity's temporal footprint must relate to a window `[start, end)`. For an event this
is its timestamp; for a trace/object it's the related event timestamps, `span` = `[first, last]`.

oneOf.description: At least one event falls inside the window.
Every event falls inside the window.
The whole span lies inside the window (`first >= start`, `last < end`).
The span covers the whole window (`first <= start`, `last >= end`).
The span's first event falls inside the window.
The span's last event falls inside the window.
The span overlaps the window at all.
The span ends before the window starts.
The span starts at or after the window ends.

MatchQuantifier.description:
How related entities (events / objects) must satisfy a sub-condition in an
`EventMatch` / `ObjectMatch` predicate.

oneOf.description: At least one related entity matches.
Every related entity matches (false if there are none).
The earliest related event matches (events are time-sorted; for objects = first).
The latest related event matches (for objects = last in relation order).

SampleAmount.description: How much to sample in a Sample transform.

oneOf.description: A fixed absolute count
A percentage of the total (0.0-100.0)

SampleTarget.description: What to sample in a Sample transform.

oneOf.description: Sample traces (XES) or objects (OCEL)
Sample individual events

AttributeScope.description: Where an attribute lives in a dataset.

return_type.description: Aggregated event counts per timestamp bin, grouped by activity.

events_per_timestamp.description: Event counts per bin timestamp (millis) per activity name.

activities.description: All distinct activity names found in the log.

bin_width_ms.description:
Width of each bin in milliseconds, which is also the spacing of the bin centers.

Bins are keyed by their center, so one spans
`[center - bin_width_ms / 2, center + bin_width_ms / 2)`. `0` means there are no bins.

name: get_object_attribute_changes
docs: Extract the attribute change history for a specific object.
Returns one trace per attribute, each containing the timestamped values
in the order they appear in the log. Returns an error if the object ID
is not found.

return_type.title: ObjectAttributeChanges
return_type.description: Time-stamped attribute change history for a single OCEL object.

traces.description:
Attribute change traces keyed by attribute name.

Each entry contains the chronological list of value changes
for that attribute.

AttributeChange.description: A single attribute value change at a point in time.

value.description: Attribute value at this point in time.

name: locel_oc_perf_sojourn_per_event
docs: Per-event sojourn time.
For each event with at least one directly-follows predecessor, the sojourn time is
`event_time - latest_predecessor_time` in integer microseconds. Returns one row
`(event_id, sojourn_us)` per qualifying event.
`top_k`: if `Some(k)`, return only the `k` rows with the largest `sojourn_us`, ties broken by
ascending event id, sorted descending. `None` returns every qualifying event.

name: locel_oc_perf_sync_per_event
docs: Per-event synchronization time and the delaying object.
For each event with at least one directly-follows predecessor, the synchronization time is
`max_predecessor_time - min_predecessor_time` in integer microseconds (the span between its
earliest and latest directly-preceding event). The delaying object is the object linking the
latest predecessor (ties broken by ascending object id).
Returns one row `(event_id, sync_us, delaying_object_id)` per qualifying event.
`top_k`: if `Some(k)`, return only the `k` rows with the largest `sync_us`, ties broken by
ascending event id, sorted descending. `None` returns every qualifying event.

name: locel_conversion_rate
docs: Conversion rate from `source_type` to `target_type` via O2O, restricted to targets touched by `activity`.
Returns the fraction of `source_type` objects that have at least one outgoing O2O edge to a
`target_type` object related (via E2O) to some event of the given event type. Returns `0.0`
if no `source_type` objects exist.

name: locel_event_object_type_counts
docs: Count E2O relationships per `(event_type, object_type)` pair.
Each entry is `(event_type, object_type, count)`. A single `(event, object)` pair connected
by multiple qualifiers contributes once per qualifier. Pairs with zero relations are omitted.
Result row order is unspecified.

name: extraction_column_domain_items
docs: Every distinct value of `table.column` in a source held in the registry.
The registry counterpart of `extraction_column_domain`: same answer, for a source whose bytes
the host already holds rather than one reachable by connection string. Without it a dropped
file could be extracted from but never inspected, so the editor could not offer the example
values a dynamic type name needs, and on wasm, where every source is byte-held, not at all.
`sources` maps source id to registry item id. Every entry other than `source_id` is ignored.

name: extraction_compile
docs: Compile `blueprint` into SQL views presenting the OCEL 2.0 surface over `catalog`'s tables,
with no connection opened and no row read.
`shape` picks the emitted layout: [`EmissionShape::PerType`] (one view per declared event/
object type, the layout external OCEL 2.0 tooling reads) or [`EmissionShape::Consolidated`]
(a single wide `events`/`objects`/... layout with the type as a column value). A mapping the
emitter cannot reproduce exactly is skipped and recorded in the result rather than failing the
whole compile.

on_duplicate_object.description: What to do about a repeated object id.

oneOf.description: Use the id expression's value verbatim.

Prefix the id with its type name, so ids from different types cannot collide.

Under this setting every relation endpoint must declare its type, since otherwise the
prefixed id cannot be rebuilt. Validation enforces that.

label.description: Display label. No semantic role.

Inner-join two nodes on the given column pairs.

Concatenate the rows of several nodes, aligning columns by name.

`UNION ALL`, not `UNION`: dropping duplicates would drop the entities they produce. Output
columns are the union of the inputs' column names, and an input lacking one contributes
`Null`. Both are model semantics a compiler must reproduce.

inputs.description: Input node ids.

Predicate.description:
A boolean test over one row.

Comparisons are typed: numbers compare numerically, so `amount > 0` means what it says
rather than comparing text. Any comparison involving `NULL` is false, including `NULL = NULL`.

oneOf.description: All conditions hold. An empty list is true.
Any condition holds. An empty list is false.
The condition does not hold.
Compare two operands.
The column is `NULL` or absent.

The column's text (see [`Value::display_string`]) matches the regular expression.
The column equals one of the listed literals.
The value in a column of the current row.
A fixed value.

Literal.description:
A literal in a comparison or membership test.

Untagged in JSON, so `true`, `5`, `5.0` and `"x"` deserialize to the matching variant.

with each other (a bare JSON boolean, number or string): boolean before integer before float
before text.

rather than a bare string, so its position does not matter and no ordinary string that happens
to parse as RFC 3339 is silently reclassified. A plain string against a timestamp column works
without it, through `Predicate::prepare`'s literal coercion.

anyOf.description: An instant with a fixed UTC offset, given as RFC 3339 text.

oneOf.description: Equal.
Not equal.
Less than.
Less than or equal.
Greater than.
Greater than or equal.

MappingEntry.description:
A mapping, or an ordered group of them.

`Single` is not boxed: it is the overwhelmingly common case, and callers construct and match
it directly.

oneOf.description: One independent mapping.

Mappings tried in order, where the first match wins.

Surface sugar: desugaring rewrites each guard to exclude the earlier ones, so nothing
downstream of validation sees this variant.

Target.description: What a mapping produces from a row.

oneOf.description: An event.

be compiled to a view.

id makes one event per item, an id naming the order one event per order, still related
to every item. The repeated rows count as
[`MappingStats::deduplicated`](super::report::MappingStats::deduplicated) while
`objects` below is emitted for each.

oneOf.description: An object.

timestamp.description:
When the attribute values below were observed. `None` records them as static
values stamped at the Unix epoch.

oneOf.description: An event-to-object relation.
An object-to-object relation.

ValueExpression.description:
Produces one text value from a row.

Used by every position that becomes an identity: entity ids, relation endpoints, type names
and qualifiers. Every variant propagates absence, so if any input has no

oneOf.description: The value in a column.
A fixed string.
Text with `{column}` placeholders, for example `ORD-{order_id}-{region}`.
The first part that produces a value.

TimestampSource.description:
Where an entity's timestamp comes from.

`deny_unknown_fields`: a misspelled key would otherwise be ignored, leaving a timestamp that
silently drops every row.

oneOf.description: One value: a column, a constant, a template or a coalesce, with a format.

format.description: How to read it. `None` means auto-detection.

oneOf.description:
Separate date and time parts, combined.

Required by schemas that split them: `ERPNext`'s `posting_date` plus `posting_time`,

date.description: Where the date comes from, if anywhere.

time.description: Where the time comes from, if anywhere.

TimestampFormat.description: How to interpret a timestamp value.

oneOf.description: Try a cascade of common formats, most specific first.
A `chrono` format string.
Seconds since the Unix epoch.
Milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

TimestampPart.description: One value read as a timestamp: where the text comes from, and how to read it.

format.description: How to read it. `None` means auto-detection.

AttributeMapping.description: Maps a source column to a named OCEL attribute.

name.description: Attribute name in the resulting log.

value_type.description: Declared attribute type, or `None` to take the catalog's type for `source_column`.

oneOf.description: String
`DateTime`
Integer
Float
Boolean
Placeholder for invalid types

InlineObjectRef.description: An object related to an event declared by the same mapping.

ObjectEndpoint.description: A reference to an object, used at every position where one is named.

object_type.description:
The object's type. Required under [`IdRendering::TypePrefixed`] and under
[`MissingEndpointPolicy::Create`].

split.description: Split the id cell into several ids, producing one relation per part.

SplitSpec.description: How to split one cell into several values.

kind.description: The splitting rule.

trim.description: Trim surrounding whitespace from each part.

oneOf.description: Split on a literal separator.

Extract values with a regular expression.

With capture groups, every group of every match yields a value. Without them, each whole

EventEndpoint.description: A reference to an event. Mirrors [`ObjectEndpoint`].

Mapping.description: One mapping from a node's rows to entities.

node.description: The node whose rows this reads.

label.description: Display label, also used to name this mapping in diagnostics.

when.description: Only rows satisfying this produce anything. `None` accepts every row.

MissingEndpointPolicy.description: What to do when a relation names an entity that does not exist.

oneOf.description: Skip the relation.
Create the object. Requires the endpoint to declare its type.
Record an error.

DuplicateObjectPolicy.description: What to do when an object id is produced more than once.

oneOf.description: Keep the first, and count the rest as deduplicated rather than lost.
Record an error.

args.title: ExtractionCatalog
args.description:
The concrete, serializable [`Catalog`].

This is the form that crosses a bindings boundary, that an editor holds and sends back, and
that gets pinned to disk so a compile can be reproduced against a schema that has since
changed.

tables.description: Table schemas, keyed by source id then table name.

domains.description: Column domains, keyed by source id, then table name, then column name.

previews.description:
A handful of real rows per table, keyed by source id then table name, to show a person
what the data looks like.

Deliberately unreachable through the [`Catalog`] trait: unlike
[`domains`](ExtractionCatalog::domains), a preview is incomplete, so compiling from one
would emit views only for the types that happened to appear first.

name.description: Table name.
Column name.

col_type.description: The source's own type name, verbatim, for example `INTEGER` or `timestamp`.

TablePreview.description:
A few real rows of one table, for display only.

Rows are aligned to [`TablePreview::columns`] so a wide table can be read across. A cell is
`None` for SQL `NULL`, distinct from `Some(String::new())`.

columns.description: Column names, in the order the rows are aligned to.

rows.description: Rows, each the same length as `columns`.

args.title: EmissionShape
args.description: Which OCEL surface the compiler emits.

oneOf.description:
One `event_<T>` / `object_<T>` view per declared type, plus `event`, `object`,
`event_object`, `object_object` and the two type maps: the OCEL 2.0 layout external tooling
reads.

The `events`/`objects`/`e2o`/`o2o`/`object_attribute_changes`/`event_attr_meta` layout
`rust4pm`'s own reader (`DuckDbLinkedOCEL`) consumes. A type is stored as a column value
rather than encoded into a view name, so no
[`Catalog::column_domain`] lookup is needed and
[`RejectReason::DynamicTypeName`] never fires.

args.title: SqlDialect
args.description:
Which SQL engine the emitted statements target.

The two are not equally evidenced: `DuckDb` is checked row-for-row against the extractor by
the differential suite, while `Postgres` is only covered by unit tests over the emitted text.

oneOf.description: `DuckDB`, the engine the differential tests run against.
`PostgreSQL` 12+. Emitted from the same fragments as `DuckDb`, see the type-level note.

return_type.title: CompiledOcel
return_type.description:
A blueprint compiled to SQL.

Serializable but not deserializable: [`Self::errors`] holds [`CompileError`], which is not, so
neither is this. Crosses a bindings boundary outbound only, as a compile binding's return
value.

SqlDialect.description:
Which SQL engine the emitted statements target.

The two are not equally evidenced: `DuckDb` is checked row-for-row against the extractor by
the differential suite, while `Postgres` is only covered by unit tests over the emitted text.

oneOf.description: `DuckDB`, the engine the differential tests run against.
`PostgreSQL` 12+. Emitted from the same fragments as `DuckDb`, see the type-level note.

EmissionShape.description: Which OCEL surface the compiler emits.

oneOf.description:
One `event_<T>` / `object_<T>` view per declared type, plus `event`, `object`,
`event_object`, `object_object` and the two type maps: the OCEL 2.0 layout external tooling
reads.

The `events`/`objects`/`e2o`/`o2o`/`object_attribute_changes`/`event_attr_meta` layout
`rust4pm`'s own reader (`DuckDbLinkedOCEL`) consumes. A type is stored as a column value
rather than encoded into a view name, so no
[`Catalog::column_domain`] lookup is needed and
[`RejectReason::DynamicTypeName`] never fires.

ViewDef.description: One compiled relation: a name and the bare `SELECT` that defines it.

name.description: The relation's name, unquoted.

body.description:
A bare `SELECT` body with no `CREATE` wrapper, so the same text serves a view, a CTE and
a `CREATE TABLE AS`.

Probe.description:
A data-dependent assumption the compiled relations make, as SQL that returns zero rows when
the assumption holds.

mapping.description: The mapping this is about, or `None` for a whole-log check.

kind.description: What it guards.

sql.description: The check itself, as a `SELECT` returning zero rows when the guard holds.

MappingRef.description: Points a diagnostic back at the mapping it came from.

index.description: Position in the desugared, flattened mapping list this run executed.

label.description: The mapping's own label, if it has one.

path.description:
The JSON path of the authored entry this mapping came from (see `desugar_with_paths`), so
a diagnostic points at what the author wrote rather than a position in the flattened
list.

describes.description:
What this mapping produces, derived from its target: `event "appoint officer"`,
`event -> object relation`, and so on. Present whether or not a `label` was typed.

oneOf.description:
Two objects claim one id under different types. The extractor keeps the first and reports
the collision, and the views keep both.
Two events claim one id. See [`Self::AmbiguousObjectIdentity`].

Two rows of one mapping give one object id different static attribute values. The
extractor writes the mapping's first row for an id and ignores later repeats. SQL rows
are unordered, so the views agree only when the repeats carry the same values.

A type name read from a column has a value outside the domain the catalog supplied, so
the compiled view set is missing the entities carrying it.

column.description: The column the domain came from.

CompileError.description:
A mapping that produced no view, and why.

Compilation never fails wholesale: an uncompilable mapping is skipped and recorded here, and
everything else still compiles.

Serializable but not deserializable: [`RejectReason`] is not, so neither is this.

mapping.description: The mapping this is about, or `None` for a blueprint-level problem.

reason.description: Why it could not be compiled.

RejectReason.description:
Why a mapping could not be compiled to a view. Every variant names something the emitter
refused to guess at.

Serializable but not deserializable: several variants carry `&'static str` fields, so this only
ever crosses a bindings boundary outbound.

oneOf.description:
A `Target::Event` with no `id` expression: the extractor mints a fresh `UUID` per row, a
nondeterministic side effect with no relational denotation.

A type name is read from the data and the catalog supplies no domain for the column it
comes from, so there is no name to put in `CREATE VIEW event_<T>`.

field.description: The position whose type is dynamic.

oneOf.description:
A column domain has more distinct values than [`MAX_TYPE_DOMAIN`], so a per-type shape
would emit one view per value.

column.description: The column the domain came from.

size.description: How many values it has.

oneOf.description: A type name collides with one of the relations the emitter itself defines.

name.description: The offending type name.

oneOf.description: A mapping reads a node that is not declared.
A node's column shape could not be resolved, typically because of an unknown source table.
The node graph contains a cycle, so there is no order in which to emit it.

node.description: A node id taking part in the cycle.

oneOf.description: A node has no columns, and SQL has no zero-column `SELECT`.
A `Union` node with no inputs.
An expression reads a column the node does not have.

The catalog's `col_type` for a column maps to no
[`ValueKind`](super::value::ValueKind), so the rule the extractor applies to that
column's values cannot be decided at compile time.

A `Float` or `Timestamp` column, which has no
[`Value::canonical_string`](super::value::Value::canonical_string), is used at an identity
position, where it makes the expression `None` for every row.

A column whose [`Value::display_string`](super::value::Value::display_string) a SQL cast
does not reproduce feeds a position that reads it as text. Rust writes `1` where `DuckDB`
writes `1.0`, and keeps a timestamp's original offset.
A timestamp is parsed by a `chrono` cascade that is not translated to SQL.

A join key column's declared kind is unknown, so whether the extractor's kind-tagged keys
can match is not decidable at compile time.

side.description: Which side the column is on.

oneOf.description: A regular expression does not compile at all.

A `Template` has an unterminated or empty placeholder, which makes it `None` for every
row.

An attribute's declared type is not the source column's kind, and the coercion
`attribute_value` applies is not one a typed SQL column can reproduce: its fallback on
failure is the cell's own natural value, which has a different type.

A mapping whose type name comes from the data declares an attribute that another mapping
declares under a different type. A statically-named type has its declarations reconciled
before the first row. A data-named one declares lazily, one row at a time, so which type
wins depends on row order.

A relation view's dependencies on other relation views form a cycle, so no order exists
in which its `CREATE VIEW` (or CTE, or `CREATE TABLE ... AS`) could run. Only reachable
from a blueprint that skipped [`validate`](super::validate()).

The blueprint does not [`validate`](super::validate::validate) against the catalog, so
nothing was compiled. One per
[`ValidationError`](super::validate::ValidationError), rendered through its `Display`.

`ocel-sqlite`. `sources` maps each `source_id` a blueprint names to the registry id of an
imported source file.

name: extraction_run_items
docs: Run `blueprint` against sources held in the registry, returning the resulting log.
Returns a fresh `SlimLinkedOCEL` rather than filling one given by `&mut`, because a binding
cannot both take a `&mut` big type and read the registry: the `&mut` borrow of the state guard
is live across the call, so lending the same guard out as a [`StateRef`] would not borrow-check.
The [`ExtractionReport`] (drop reasons, per-mapping counts) is not returned, because a binding
returns either a big type or plain data, never both. A run whose report carries errors
therefore fails with them rather than handing back a log that silently lost rows. Validate
first with [`extraction_validate`] to catch what a report would otherwise tell you.

name: extraction_validate
docs: Check `blueprint` against `catalog` for problems decidable from the schema alone, such as an
unknown source or table, a node graph cycle, or a type-rendering rule the blueprint's own
`id_rendering` setting cannot satisfy.
An empty result means `blueprint` is safe to pass to [`extraction_run`],
[`extraction_run_to_duckdb`] or [`extraction_compile`]. All three call this internally and
refuse to run an invalid blueprint, so calling it first is for surfacing errors to a user
while they edit, not a required step before the others.
The two report a refusal differently, because they fail differently: the running bindings
return an error string, while [`extraction_compile`] always returns a [`CompiledOcel`] and
puts one entry per validation error in its `errors` array, with no relations emitted. This is
also the only place a blueprint's `version` is checked: the bindings deserialize a
[`Blueprint`] with plain serde, not `Blueprint::from_json`, so a blueprint from a newer model
version is caught here and nowhere else.

[`errors_suppressed`](Self::errors_suppressed).

errors_suppressed.description:
Non-fatal problems the run hit past [`MAX_REPORTED_ERRORS`], which
[`errors`](Self::errors) therefore does not name. Zero for every run under the cap.

rows_materialized.description:
Rows every `Join`/`Union` materialization this run performed produced, summed across
materializations rather than peaked: an upper bound on peak buffered rows. A cached
materialization is counted once, when computed.

Zero when no mapping's node graph contains a `Join` or `Union`, since a pure
`Source -> Filter` chain streams. Zero is therefore a witness that the run streamed.

pushdown_declined.description:
Nodes whose source could have executed the whole node but the compiler declined to build
the query for, paired with the reason, and deduplicated per node.

Always safe, since the executor runs the node itself. Reported because falling back on a
`Join` is the one execution path whose memory grows with the data, so this explains a
non-zero [`rows_materialized`](Self::rows_materialized).

finalize.description:
What the sink did at [`ExtractionSink::finalize`](super::sink::ExtractionSink::finalize).

All zero for a sink that resolves relation endpoints eagerly, which reports everything
through [`per_mapping`](Self::per_mapping) instead. See
[`Resolution`](super::sink::Resolution).

timing.description:
Where the run's wall-clock time went.

`None` from [`extract`](super::extract::extract) itself, which is handed open providers
and cannot know what they cost to obtain. The runner that owns the connections fills this
in, as the `extraction-dbcon` bindings do. Also kept out of `extract` because
`std::time::Instant` panics on `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.

rows_read.description: Rows the mapping's node produced, before `when` was applied.

entities_emitted.description:
Entities or relations this mapping handed to the sink, which is not the same as
"survived the run" for a sink that defers resolution.

An eager sink refuses a dangling relation at the call site, so it lands in
[`DropReason::UnresolvedEndpoint`] and never here. A deferring sink writes it, counts it
here, and deletes it at [`finalize`](super::sink::ExtractionSink::finalize), reporting it
in [`FinalizeReport::unresolved_endpoints`](super::sink::FinalizeReport) instead. To count
what a run produced, subtract `ExtractionReport::finalize.unresolved_endpoints` from the
total.

deduplicated.description:
Rows that tried to create an entity the sink already had. Not a loss: an object mapping
at event grain names the same object on every row by design. See
[`DuplicateObjectPolicy::Error`](super::blueprint::DuplicateObjectPolicy::Error) for what
turns a repeat into a loss instead.

One increment per row whose entity-creating call found the entity already present, across
mappings, since the sink is what answers.

Resolving a relation endpoint is never counted, so an `E2O`/`O2O` mapping reports zero
however often its rows repeat an id: finding an existing endpoint is the normal successful
case. A blueprint that wants its inline references' repeats counted can name the objects
with their own [`Target::Object`](super::blueprint::Target::Object) mapping.

dropped.description:
Rows dropped, by reason. A row that matches several reasons at once (rare) is counted
once, under the first one detected.

uncoercible_attributes.description:
Attribute values that would not convert to their attribute's declared type, stored as
`Null`. Not a dropped row: the entity was written, with one of its attributes empty.

MappingRef.description: Points a diagnostic back at the mapping it came from.

index.description: Position in the desugared, flattened mapping list this run executed.

label.description: The mapping's own label, if it has one.

path.description:
The JSON path of the authored entry this mapping came from (see `desugar_with_paths`), so
a diagnostic points at what the author wrote rather than a position in the flattened
list.

describes.description:
What this mapping produces, derived from its target: `event "appoint officer"`,
`event -> object relation`, and so on. Present whether or not a `label` was typed.

ExtractionError.description:
Why [`extract`](super::extract::extract) could not run at all, or a non-fatal problem
recorded in [`ExtractionReport::errors`] while it did.

Serializable but not deserializable: some variants carry `&'static str` fields (a borrow no
deserializer can manufacture), so this only ever crosses a bindings boundary outbound.

oneOf.description:
The blueprint failed [`validate`](super::validate::validate), so `extract` refuses to run
it. Fatal.

A `Source` node names a `source_id` with no entry in the `providers` map `extract` was
given. Fatal.

A predicate's or split's regular expression failed to compile. Fatal. `validate` checks
this, so it should not happen when `extract` is called on a validated blueprint.

A `Join`'s `on` clause named a key column that its input's rows do not carry. Fatal:
dropping the column from the key instead would shorten it, silently turning the join into
a partial cross product.

side.description: `"left"` or `"right"`.

column.description: The key column, as named on that side.

oneOf.description:
A [`RowProvider`](super::provider::RowProvider) call failed. Fatal: the rows a mapping
needs are simply not available.

node.description: The node being read when the failure happened.

oneOf.description:
An [`ExtractionSink`](super::sink::ExtractionSink) call failed for a reason other than a
policy below. Fatal: this is the storage layer failing, and carrying on would leave a
half-written OCEL that reports success.

context.description: What was being added when the failure happened.

oneOf.description:
Two mappings, or two rows, produced the same rendered id under two different types.
Only reachable under [`IdRendering::Raw`](super::blueprint::IdRendering::Raw). Non-fatal:
the row is dropped (see [`DropReason::IdTypeCollision`]) and the run continues, since
merging the two would fold two distinct entities into one.

requested_type.description:
The type this row wanted the id for. The type that already holds it is whatever the
sink reports for that id.

oneOf.description:
Two mappings declared the same attribute of the same entity type under different value
types. Non-fatal: the declaration is widened to a type covering both (see
[`OCELAttributeType::coalesce`](crate::core::event_data::object_centric::OCELAttributeType::coalesce))
and every row converted to it. Reported because the resulting type is then decided by a
coincidence of two mappings rather than by either author's intent. Names no mapping: the
conflict is a property of the pair.

kind.description: `"event"` or `"object"`.

declared.description: The type it was declared with first.

conflicting.description: The type the later declaration gave it.

oneOf.description: `on_duplicate_object: Error` fired: `id` had already been added by `mapping`. Non-fatal.

mapping.description: The mapping whose row named the repeat.

oneOf.description:
`on_missing_endpoint: Error` fired: `endpoint` named `id`, which could not be resolved.
Non-fatal.

mapping.description: The mapping whose row named the endpoint.

oneOf.description:
`on_missing_endpoint: Error` fired for a sink that answered
[`Resolution::Deferred`](super::sink::Resolution::Deferred): the same policy violation as
[`MissingEndpoint`](Self::MissingEndpoint), reported once for the whole run instead of
once per endpoint. Non-fatal.

Such a sink detects the violation at [`finalize`](super::sink::ExtractionSink::finalize),
where the mapping and row that named the endpoint are gone, so this names neither.

count.description:
How many relations the sink could not resolve. Usually equals an eager sink's
[`MissingEndpoint`](Self::MissingEndpoint) count for the same run, but can exceed it:
a deferring sink also stages the inline references of a `Target::Event` whose event
this run dropped, which an eager sink never asks about.

ValidationError.description: A reason a blueprint cannot be executed or compiled.

oneOf.description: The blueprint's `version` is newer than this build understands.

supported.description: The newest version this build reads.

oneOf.description: Two nodes share an id.
A node or mapping names a node that does not exist.
The node graph contains a cycle, so no evaluation order exists.

id.description: One node id participating in the cycle.

oneOf.description: A source node names a source with no entry in the catalog.
A source node names a table with no schema in the catalog.
An expression reads a column absent from the declared schema.

node.description: The node whose rows were being read.

oneOf.description: Type prefixing is on, but a relation endpoint does not declare its type.

mapping.description: Which mapping, by label or index.

oneOf.description: Missing endpoints are created, but an object endpoint does not declare its type.

mapping.description: Which mapping, by label or index.

oneOf.description: A union has no inputs, so it has no columns to project.
A regular expression does not compile.

A `Template` expression has a placeholder that is unterminated or empty, either of which
drops every row instead of the intended substitution.

A `Join` output column resolves to no single input column: the left input has a column
literally named `right_<name>` and the right input's `<name>` is renamed onto it.

A comparison literal cannot be read as the type its column declares, so the comparison
matches no row at all, however the data looks.

Raised only where the column's declared type names a kind: an unrecognized `col_type` turns
coercion off on purpose, and then the literal is compared as authored.

location.description: The mapping, by label or authored path, or the `Filter` node, the comparison sits in.

col_type.description: That column's declared type, verbatim from the catalog.

oneOf.description:
A comparison's two operands (both columns, or both literals) have different, statically
known kinds that [`Value::compare`](super::value::Value::compare) has no rule for (only
`integer`/`float` compare across kinds), so it matches no row at all.

location.description: The mapping, by label or authored path, or the `Filter` node, the comparison sits in.

left_kind.description: The left operand's declared kind: `text`, `integer`, `float`, `boolean` or `timestamp`.

oneOf.description: `table` has no entry in this provider.
A requested column is not present on `table`.

This provider cannot execute SQL: it reports no [`RowProvider::query_dialect`], or the
query it was handed is one it cannot run. Not fatal: the caller falls back to executing
the node row by row.
The underlying source failed while reading.

table.description: The table being read when the failure happened.

SinkError.description:
Why an [`ExtractionSink`] call failed.

Serializable but not deserializable: [`SinkError::UnknownType`] carries a `&'static str` (a
borrow no deserializer can manufacture), so this only ever crosses a bindings boundary
outbound, nested inside [`ExtractionError::Sink`](super::report::ExtractionError::Sink).

oneOf.description: [`ExtractionSink::add_event`] was called with an id already present.
[`ExtractionSink::add_object`] was called with an id already present.

[`ExtractionSink::add_object`] was called for `id`, but `id` is already present under a
different object type, i.e. two distinct entities collided on one id rather than the plain
repeat [`SinkError::DuplicateObject`] reports. Only reachable under
[`IdRendering::Raw`](super::blueprint::IdRendering::Raw). A deferring sink cannot make that
distinction at [`resolve_object`](ExtractionSink::resolve_object) time and reports it
here.

An entity was added, or a relation named an endpoint, under a type that was never
declared via [`ExtractionSink::declare_event_type`] / [`declare_object_type`](ExtractionSink::declare_object_type).

kind.description: `"event"` or `"object"`.

name.description: The undeclared type name.

oneOf.description:
A relation named a ref this sink instance did not itself hand out. Cannot happen through
[`extract`](super::extract::extract).
The backend failed (I/O, driver error), as its message.
String
`DateTime`
Integer
Float
Boolean
Placeholder for invalid types

PushdownDeclined.description: One node the compiler refused to push down to its source, and why.

node.description: The node id, as the blueprint names it.

RejectReason.description:
Why a mapping could not be compiled to a view. Every variant names something the emitter
refused to guess at.

Serializable but not deserializable: several variants carry `&'static str` fields, so this only
ever crosses a bindings boundary outbound.

oneOf.description:
A `Target::Event` with no `id` expression: the extractor mints a fresh `UUID` per row, a
nondeterministic side effect with no relational denotation.

A type name is read from the data and the catalog supplies no domain for the column it
comes from, so there is no name to put in `CREATE VIEW event_<T>`.

field.description: The position whose type is dynamic.

oneOf.description:
A column domain has more distinct values than [`MAX_TYPE_DOMAIN`], so a per-type shape
would emit one view per value.

column.description: The column the domain came from.

size.description: How many values it has.

oneOf.description: A type name collides with one of the relations the emitter itself defines.

name.description: The offending type name.

oneOf.description: A mapping reads a node that is not declared.
A node's column shape could not be resolved, typically because of an unknown source table.
The node graph contains a cycle, so there is no order in which to emit it.

node.description: A node id taking part in the cycle.

oneOf.description: A node has no columns, and SQL has no zero-column `SELECT`.
A `Union` node with no inputs.
An expression reads a column the node does not have.

The catalog's `col_type` for a column maps to no
[`ValueKind`](super::value::ValueKind), so the rule the extractor applies to that
column's values cannot be decided at compile time.

A `Float` or `Timestamp` column, which has no
[`Value::canonical_string`](super::value::Value::canonical_string), is used at an identity
position, where it makes the expression `None` for every row.

A column whose [`Value::display_string`](super::value::Value::display_string) a SQL cast
does not reproduce feeds a position that reads it as text. Rust writes `1` where `DuckDB`
writes `1.0`, and keeps a timestamp's original offset.
A timestamp is parsed by a `chrono` cascade that is not translated to SQL.

A join key column's declared kind is unknown, so whether the extractor's kind-tagged keys
can match is not decidable at compile time.

side.description: Which side the column is on.

oneOf.description: A regular expression does not compile at all.

A `Template` has an unterminated or empty placeholder, which makes it `None` for every
row.

An attribute's declared type is not the source column's kind, and the coercion
`attribute_value` applies is not one a typed SQL column can reproduce: its fallback on
failure is the cell's own natural value, which has a different type.

A mapping whose type name comes from the data declares an attribute that another mapping
declares under a different type. A statically-named type has its declarations reconciled
before the first row. A data-named one declares lazily, one row at a time, so which type
wins depends on row order.

A relation view's dependencies on other relation views form a cycle, so no order exists
in which its `CREATE VIEW` (or CTE, or `CREATE TABLE ... AS`) could run. Only reachable
from a blueprint that skipped [`validate`](super::validate()).

The blueprint does not [`validate`](super::validate::validate) against the catalog, so
nothing was compiled. One per
[`ValidationError`](super::validate::ValidationError), rendered through its `Display`.

FinalizeReport.description:
What a sink did during [`ExtractionSink::finalize`], folded into
[`ExtractionReport::finalize`](super::report::ExtractionReport::finalize).

All zero for a sink that resolves eagerly. Nonzero entries carry a deferring sink's share of
the per-mapping counters.

resolved_relations.description:
Relations written against a [`Resolution::Deferred`] endpoint that resolved to a real
entity at finalize.

unresolved_endpoints.description:
Relations whose deferred endpoint did not resolve. An eager sink counts these per mapping
as [`DropReason::UnresolvedEndpoint`](super::report::DropReason::UnresolvedEndpoint).

objects_created.description:
Objects synthesized at finalize under `on_missing_endpoint: Create`, for deferred
endpoints that turned out not to exist.

duplicates_removed.description:
Repeated entity ids removed at finalize: a deferring sink's share of
[`MappingStats::deduplicated`](super::report::MappingStats::deduplicated).

ExtractionTiming.description:
How long a run spent, split by phase, in milliseconds. Schema discovery is a fixed cost a
caller holding a catalog can skip, so it is reported apart from the row reading.

discovery_ms.description: Connecting to each source and reading its schema. Zero when the caller supplied a catalog.

extraction_ms.description: Reading rows and emitting entities: `extract` itself.

name: extraction_table_preview
docs: The first `limit` rows of `table` in the source named `source_id`, for showing a person what
the data looks like while they build a blueprint against it.
Not a substitute for [`extraction_column_domain`]: a preview is incomplete, so it must never
be used where the compiler needs a column's full domain.
`connections` must contain an entry for `source_id`. Every other entry is ignored.

name: locel_new
docs: Create a new empty [`SlimLinkedOCEL`].
A [`SlimLinkedOCEL`] is an object-centric event log where events and objects are referenced
by integer indices ([`EventIndex`] / [`ObjectIndex`]) returned from the `add_*` calls,
and each indexed event/object is an instance of an event/object type (activity / object class)
declared beforehand with an ordered list of attributes.

args.title: output_id
args.description: Store the result under this id instead of a generated one.

name: locel_oc_perf_sojourn_per_event
docs: Per-event sojourn time.
For each event with at least one directly-follows predecessor, the sojourn time is
`event_time - latest_predecessor_time` in integer microseconds. Returns one row
`(event_id, sojourn_us)` per qualifying event.
`top_k`: if `Some(k)`, return only the `k` rows with the largest `sojourn_us`, ties broken by
ascending event id, sorted descending. `None` returns every qualifying event.

name: locel_oc_perf_sync_per_event
docs: Per-event synchronization time and the delaying object.
For each event with at least one directly-follows predecessor, the synchronization time is
`max_predecessor_time - min_predecessor_time` in integer microseconds (the span between its
earliest and latest directly-preceding event). The delaying object is the object linking the
latest predecessor (ties broken by ascending object id).
Returns one row `(event_id, sync_us, delaying_object_id)` per qualifying event.
`top_k`: if `Some(k)`, return only the `k` rows with the largest `sync_us`, ties broken by
ascending event id, sorted descending. `None` returns every qualifying event.

args.title: InductiveMiner
args.description:
An Inductive Miner with its settings: one that recurses on the log, or the
[directly-follows variant](dfg_miner).

In JSON, `kind` tells them apart, e.g., `{"kind": "log", "noise_threshold": 0.2}` or
`{"kind": "dfg"}`, and fields left out take their default value.

oneOf.description: IM, `IMf` or `IMa`, which recurse on the log.
`IMd` or `IMfd`, which recurse on the directly-follows graph.

InductiveMinerOptions.description:
Settings of the Inductive Miner. Each constructor sets up one variant:
- [`default`](Self::default): IM
- [`imf`](Self::imf): `IMf` with the given noise threshold
- [`ima`](Self::ima): IM with the cuts of `IMa`
- [`im_thesis`](Self::im_thesis) and [`imf_thesis`](Self::imf_thesis): IM and `IMf` as
  published, without the refinements of this implementation
- [`prom`](Self::prom) and [`pm4py`](Self::pm4py): the settings closest to those tools

Fields missing in JSON take their default value.

noise_threshold.description:
Deviation threshold `f ∈ [0, 1]` of `IMf`, clamped to that range. `0.0` turns filtering
off.

use_fallthroughs.description: Whether to try the [fall throughs](fallthrough) before resorting to a flower model.

strict_sequence.description:
Whether to merge the parts of a sequence cut that only occur together with a skippable
neighbor.

use_interleaved.description:
Whether to look for interleaved (`↔`) cuts, tried before concurrency. Under `IMf` they still
read the unfiltered traces, so noise can prevent them.

use_inclusive_choice.description:
Whether to regroup concurrent cuts into nested concurrency, optionality and inclusive
choice (`∨`).

guard_empty_cut_parts.description:
Whether to refuse a cut whose split leaves a part without any events, which only the
filtering splits of `IMf` can do, and fall through instead. Otherwise the cut is taken and
the part becomes `τ`, as in the thesis.

use_minimum_self_distance.description:
Whether concurrency detection consults the minimum-self-distance relation (∧↔.1), which
tells `a` and `b` running concurrently from `a` looping around `b`. A concurrent cut that
keeps such activities together is preferred. If there is none, the plain one is taken.

use_degenerate_tau_loops.description:
Whether to take a tau loop that cuts every trace into single events, as the thesis does.
Mining those single events gives the flower model, so this only decides whether
[`two_activities_concurrent`](fallthrough::two_activities_concurrent) gets a chance first.

filter_single_activity.description:
Whether `IMf` keeps the single-activity base case despite repetitions when single
executions dominate (§6.2.2.3). Without it any repetition ends the recursion in a loop.

filter_activity_concurrent_probe.description:
Whether the [activity-concurrent fall through](fallthrough::activity_concurrent) also
accepts a candidate whose remaining log only has a cut after filtering. The thesis
(§6.2.2.4) probes the unfiltered graph.

keep_at_threshold.description:
Whether `IMf` keeps an edge, a start or end activity, or the empty traces, when their
frequency is exactly at the threshold.

filter_start_end.description: Whether `IMf` also removes infrequent start and end activities.

activity_concurrent_by_name.description:
Whether the [activity-concurrent fall through](fallthrough::activity_concurrent) tries the
activities by name instead of the most frequent first. It takes the first whose removal
leaves a cut.

fold.description:
Whether to [fold](crate::core::process_models::process_tree::Node::fold) the tree, e.g.,
`→(→(a, b), c)` into `→(a, b, c)` and `→(τ, a)` into `a`.

InductiveMinerDfgOptions.description:
Settings of the DFG variant of the Inductive Miner. Settings that need traces, such as the
interleaved cut, do not exist here.

Fields missing in JSON take their default value.

noise_threshold.description: Deviation threshold `f ∈ [0, 1]` of `IMfd`, clamped to that range. `0.0` is plain `IMd`.

strict_sequence.description:
Whether to merge the parts of a sequence cut that only occur together with a skippable
neighbor.

fold.description:
Whether to collapse nested occurrences of the same associative operator, turning, e.g.,
`→(→(a, b), c)` into `→(a, b, c)`.

use_tau_loops.description: Whether to try the [tau loops](strict_dfg_tau_loop) before resorting to a flower model.

flower_accepts_empty.description:
Whether the flower model allows the empty trace, i.e., is `↺(τ, ×(a₁, ..., aₙ))` instead of
the thesis' `↺(×(a₁, ..., aₙ), τ)`. The empty-traces step runs before any fall through, so
allowing one here only loses precision.

repeated_activity_to_flower.description:
Whether a lone activity with a self edge becomes a flower instead of `↺(a, τ)`. The
thesis hands the case to [`strict_dfg_tau_loop`] (§6.6.3.3). With
[`flower_accepts_empty`](Self::flower_accepts_empty), this turns `a⁺` into `a*`.

args.title: InductiveMiner
args.description:
An Inductive Miner with its settings: one that recurses on the log, or the
[directly-follows variant](dfg_miner).

In JSON, `kind` tells them apart, e.g., `{"kind": "log", "noise_threshold": 0.2}` or
`{"kind": "dfg"}`, and fields left out take their default value.

oneOf.description: IM, `IMf` or `IMa`, which recurse on the log.
`IMd` or `IMfd`, which recurse on the directly-follows graph.

InductiveMinerOptions.description:
Settings of the Inductive Miner. Each constructor sets up one variant:
- [`default`](Self::default): IM
- [`imf`](Self::imf): `IMf` with the given noise threshold
- [`ima`](Self::ima): IM with the cuts of `IMa`
- [`im_thesis`](Self::im_thesis) and [`imf_thesis`](Self::imf_thesis): IM and `IMf` as
  published, without the refinements of this implementation
- [`prom`](Self::prom) and [`pm4py`](Self::pm4py): the settings closest to those tools

Fields missing in JSON take their default value.

noise_threshold.description:
Deviation threshold `f ∈ [0, 1]` of `IMf`, clamped to that range. `0.0` turns filtering
off.

use_fallthroughs.description: Whether to try the [fall throughs](fallthrough) before resorting to a flower model.

strict_sequence.description:
Whether to merge the parts of a sequence cut that only occur together with a skippable
neighbor.

use_interleaved.description:
Whether to look for interleaved (`↔`) cuts, tried before concurrency. Under `IMf` they still
read the unfiltered traces, so noise can prevent them.

use_inclusive_choice.description:
Whether to regroup concurrent cuts into nested concurrency, optionality and inclusive
choice (`∨`).

guard_empty_cut_parts.description:
Whether to refuse a cut whose split leaves a part without any events, which only the
filtering splits of `IMf` can do, and fall through instead. Otherwise the cut is taken and
the part becomes `τ`, as in the thesis.

use_minimum_self_distance.description:
Whether concurrency detection consults the minimum-self-distance relation (∧↔.1), which
tells `a` and `b` running concurrently from `a` looping around `b`. A concurrent cut that
keeps such activities together is preferred. If there is none, the plain one is taken.

use_degenerate_tau_loops.description:
Whether to take a tau loop that cuts every trace into single events, as the thesis does.
Mining those single events gives the flower model, so this only decides whether
[`two_activities_concurrent`](fallthrough::two_activities_concurrent) gets a chance first.

filter_single_activity.description:
Whether `IMf` keeps the single-activity base case despite repetitions when single
executions dominate (§6.2.2.3). Without it any repetition ends the recursion in a loop.

filter_activity_concurrent_probe.description:
Whether the [activity-concurrent fall through](fallthrough::activity_concurrent) also
accepts a candidate whose remaining log only has a cut after filtering. The thesis
(§6.2.2.4) probes the unfiltered graph.

keep_at_threshold.description:
Whether `IMf` keeps an edge, a start or end activity, or the empty traces, when their
frequency is exactly at the threshold.

filter_start_end.description: Whether `IMf` also removes infrequent start and end activities.

activity_concurrent_by_name.description:
Whether the [activity-concurrent fall through](fallthrough::activity_concurrent) tries the
activities by name instead of the most frequent first. It takes the first whose removal
leaves a cut.

fold.description:
Whether to [fold](crate::core::process_models::process_tree::Node::fold) the tree, e.g.,
`→(→(a, b), c)` into `→(a, b, c)` and `→(τ, a)` into `a`.

InductiveMinerDfgOptions.description:
Settings of the DFG variant of the Inductive Miner. Settings that need traces, such as the
interleaved cut, do not exist here.

Fields missing in JSON take their default value.

noise_threshold.description: Deviation threshold `f ∈ [0, 1]` of `IMfd`, clamped to that range. `0.0` is plain `IMd`.

strict_sequence.description:
Whether to merge the parts of a sequence cut that only occur together with a skippable
neighbor.

fold.description:
Whether to collapse nested occurrences of the same associative operator, turning, e.g.,
`→(→(a, b), c)` into `→(a, b, c)`.

use_tau_loops.description: Whether to try the [tau loops](strict_dfg_tau_loop) before resorting to a flower model.

flower_accepts_empty.description:
Whether the flower model allows the empty trace, i.e., is `↺(τ, ×(a₁, ..., aₙ))` instead of
the thesis' `↺(×(a₁, ..., aₙ), τ)`. The empty-traces step runs before any fall through, so
allowing one here only loses precision.

repeated_activity_to_flower.description:
Whether a lone activity with a self edge becomes a flower instead of `↺(a, τ)`. The
thesis hands the case to [`strict_dfg_tau_loop`] (§6.6.3.3). With
[`flower_accepts_empty`](Self::flower_accepts_empty), this turns `a⁺` into `a*`.

filter_single_activity.description:
Whether `IMfd` keeps the single-activity base case despite a self edge when single
executions dominate (§6.6.4.3). Without it a self edge always ends the recursion in a loop.

name: get_dfg_of_object_type
docs: Get the directly-follows graph (DFG) for objects of the given object type.
Each entry is `((from_activity, to_activity), count)`, counting adjacent pairs in each
object's timestamp-ordered activity trace. Sorted by count descending, ties broken by

name: discover_oc_declare
docs: Discover behavioral OC-DECLARE constraints from the given OCEL

args.title: OCDeclareDiscoveryOptions
args.description: Options for the automatic discovery of OC-DECLARE constraints

noise_threshold.description: Noise threshold (i.e., what fraction of events are allowed to violate a discovered constraint)

o2o_mode.description: Determines if/how object-to-object relationships are considered

acts_to_use.description: Activities to use for the discovery. If this is `None`, all activities of the OCEL are used

object_types_to_use.description:
Object types to use for the discovery. If this is `None`, all object types of the OCEL are used

An object-to-object association is only used if both of its object types are selected.

counts_for_generation.description: What min/max counts to use for the candidate generation steps

counts_for_filter.description: What min/max counts to use for the candidate filtering step (when the arrow type is determined)

reduction.description: If/how the discovered constraints should be reduced

refinement.description: Determines if the object involvement of discovered constraints should be made more precise/strict after initial discovery and reduction

considered_arrow_types.description:
The arrow types to consider when deriving the final constraints

Should be non-empty!

O2OMode.description:
O2O Mode for OC-DECLARE Discovery

Determines to what extent object-to-object (O2O) relationships are considered

oneOf.description: O2O relationships are not considered at all
Direct O2O relationships are considered (i.e., only one direction)
Reverse direction of O2O relationships are considered
O2O relationships and their inverse directions are considered
Do not reduce constraints at all

Apply lossless reduction

i.e., only removes constraints strictly implied by combining others

Apply lossy reduction

May also remove constraints which are not implied by others

OCDeclareArcType.description:
OC-DECLARE Arc Direction/Type

Models temporal relationships

oneOf.description: Association: No temporal restrictions
Eventually-Follows: Target must occur after source event
Eventually-Precedes: Target must occur before source event
Directly-Follows: Target must occur directly after source event (considering events that involve all required objects)
Directly-Precedes: Target must occur directly before source event (considering events that involve all required objects)

Directly-Precedes: Target must occur directly before source event (considering events that involve all required objects)

OCDeclareArcLabel.description: Object Involvement Label of an OC-DECLARE arc

each.description: Each (for each object of that type separately, there must be the specified number of relevant target events)

any.description: Any (there must be the specified number of relevant target events involving at least one of the objects of this type involved in the source event)

args.title: OcpnDiscoveryOptions
args.description:
Settings for object-centric Petri net discovery.

In JSON, fields left out take their default value.

miner.description:
How the Petri net of each object type is discovered from its flattened log. The
[DFG variant](InductiveMiner::Dfg) reads each log once, which suits large logs.

object_types_to_use.description:
Object types to discover a net for. If this is `None`, every object type of the log is used.

Each type's net and variable arcs are discovered independently, so leaving a type out does
not change the nets of the others.

activities_to_use.description:
Activities to keep. If this is `None`, every activity is kept.

The other activities' events are removed from each flattened log before mining, so the
nets describe the log without them. An object left without events adds no trace.

variable_arc_tolerance.description:
Fraction of an activity's executions that may involve other than exactly one object of a
type while its arc to that type still counts as normal.

The default `0.0` is the strict reading. A small tolerance keeps data-quality noise from
making arcs variable.

Whether concurrency detection consults the minimum-self-distance relation (∧↔.1), which
tells `a` and `b` running concurrently from `a` looping around `b`. A concurrent cut that
keeps such activities together is preferred. If there is none, the plain one is taken.

use_degenerate_tau_loops.description:
Whether to take a tau loop that cuts every trace into single events, as the thesis does.
Mining those single events gives the flower model, so this only decides whether
[`two_activities_concurrent`](fallthrough::two_activities_concurrent) gets a chance first.

filter_single_activity.description:
Whether `IMf` keeps the single-activity base case despite repetitions when single
executions dominate (§6.2.2.3). Without it any repetition ends the recursion in a loop.

filter_activity_concurrent_probe.description:
Whether the [activity-concurrent fall through](fallthrough::activity_concurrent) also
accepts a candidate whose remaining log only has a cut after filtering. The thesis
(§6.2.2.4) probes the unfiltered graph.

keep_at_threshold.description:
Whether `IMf` keeps an edge, a start or end activity, or the empty traces, when their
frequency is exactly at the threshold.

filter_start_end.description: Whether `IMf` also removes infrequent start and end activities.

activity_concurrent_by_name.description:
Whether the [activity-concurrent fall through](fallthrough::activity_concurrent) tries the
activities by name instead of the most frequent first. It takes the first whose removal
leaves a cut.

fold.description:
Whether to [fold](crate::core::process_models::process_tree::Node::fold) the tree, e.g.,
`→(→(a, b), c)` into `→(a, b, c)` and `→(τ, a)` into `a`.

InductiveMinerDfgOptions.description:
Settings of the DFG variant of the Inductive Miner. Settings that need traces, such as the
interleaved cut, do not exist here.

Fields missing in JSON take their default value.

noise_threshold.description: Deviation threshold `f ∈ [0, 1]` of `IMfd`, clamped to that range. `0.0` is plain `IMd`.

strict_sequence.description:
Whether to merge the parts of a sequence cut that only occur together with a skippable
neighbor.

fold.description:
Whether to collapse nested occurrences of the same associative operator, turning, e.g.,
`→(→(a, b), c)` into `→(a, b, c)`.

use_tau_loops.description: Whether to try the [tau loops](strict_dfg_tau_loop) before resorting to a flower model.

flower_accepts_empty.description:
Whether the flower model allows the empty trace, i.e., is `↺(τ, ×(a₁, ..., aₙ))` instead of
the thesis' `↺(×(a₁, ..., aₙ), τ)`. The empty-traces step runs before any fall through, so
allowing one here only loses precision.

repeated_activity_to_flower.description:
Whether a lone activity with a self edge becomes a flower instead of `↺(a, τ)`. The
thesis hands the case to [`strict_dfg_tau_loop`] (§6.6.3.3). With
[`flower_accepts_empty`](Self::flower_accepts_empty), this turns `a⁺` into `a*`.

filter_single_activity.description:
Whether `IMfd` keeps the single-activity base case despite a self edge when single
executions dominate (§6.6.4.3). Without it a self edge always ends the recursion in a loop.

return_type.title: ObjectCentricPetriNetJson
return_type.description:
An object-centric Petri net as a flat list of places, transitions and arcs.

Transitions shared by several object types are listed once. Each arc has the object type of
its place.

places.description: The places, each belonging to one object type.

transitions.description: The transitions, each appearing once even when several object types share it.

arcs.description: The arcs, each between a place and a transition.

initial_marking.description: Tokens per place at the start, by place name.

final_marking.description: Tokens per place at the end, by place name.

JsonPlace.description: A place of one object type.

name.description: Unique among all places and transitions.

object_type.description: The object type whose tokens this place holds.

JsonTransition.description: A transition, silent if it has no label.

name.description: Unique among all places and transitions. For a labeled transition, the activity itself.

label.description: The activity, or `None` for a silent transition.

JsonArc.description: An arc from a place to a transition or the other way round.

source.description: Name of the place or transition the arc leaves.

target.description: Name of the place or transition the arc enters.

type.description: Whether the arc moves one object or a whole set of them.

weight.description: How many tokens the arc moves.

JsonArcType.description: Whether an arc moves a single object or all of them at once.

oneOf.description: Moves one object of the place's type.
Moves a set of objects of the place's type at once.

name: get_variants_of_object_type
docs: Get all activity-trace variants for objects of the given object type, with their occurrence counts
Each entry is a tuple `(activity_trace, count)`, where `activity_trace` is the sequence of event types
connected to an object (ordered by event timestamp), and `count` is the number of objects of the
requested type that share that exact trace. Sorted by count descending, ties broken by the
activity trace.

name: dfg_layout
docs: Lay the model out, returning the positions only.

args.title: DirectlyFollowsGraph
args.description:
A directly-follows graph of [`Activity`]s, with its start and end activities.
Activities and directly-follows relations are annotated with their frequency, and start and
end activities with how many traces start or end with them.

start_activities.description: Start activities, with how many traces start with each

end_activities.description: End activities, with how many traces end with each

args.title: DfgBuildOptions
args.description: How a [`DirectlyFollowsGraph`] is turned into a [`Graph`].

direction.description: Flow direction. `None` is the model's own default.

layout_patch.description:
Fields of the engine options to change, as a partial
[`LayoutOptions`](graphlay::LayoutOptions) object deep-merged over the model's preset and
the direction, e.g., `{"routing": {"style": "diagonal"}}`. `null` changes nothing.

terminals.description: Draw the artificial START / END terminals. On by default.

annotations.description: Labels, layout weights and line widths by node and edge, instead of the counts.

oneOf.description: Layers advance left to right.
Layers advance top to bottom.

LayoutOptions.description: Everything that steers one layout run.

direction.description: Which way the layers advance.

routing.description: Routing style, bundling and port choices.

coords.description: Cross-axis placement behaviour.

compaction.description: Whether and how the cross axis is compacted afterwards.

self_loops.description: How self-loops are placed and drawn.

labels.description: How edge labels are given room, and where they end up.

effort.description: How hard the engine works, as one dial. See [`Effort`].

seed.description:
Seed for the crossing minimisation's restarts and kicks. The same seed gives the same
drawing. 32 bits so it survives JSON in JavaScript. Default [`DEFAULT_SEED`].

limits.description: Input size limits. Exceeding one is an error instead of unbounded time.

wrap.description: Wrapping a long drawing into rows. Off unless a viewport shape is given.

cycles.description: Which edges of a cyclic graph are drawn against the flow.

seed_mode.description: How node positions given as seeds steer the layout.

tuning.description: The engine's internal iteration counts, budgets and thresholds. See [`Tuning`].

Spacing.description: Gaps and clearances, all in px.

layer_gap.description:
Between layer columns, on the layer axis. Default 54.

A left-to-right drawing's width grows with `n_layers * (node_w + layer_gap)`, so lower
this to narrow it.

node_gap.description: Between two real nodes in one layer, on the order axis. Default 46.

dummy_gap.description:
Between a routing track and its order-axis neighbour. Default 30, tighter than `node_gap`
because a track is a line.

port_gap.description: Minimum port-to-port separation along one border. Default 18.

port_stroke_clear.description:
Clear space between the strokes of two adjacent ports, on top of half of each stroke's
width. Default 14. Raise it for thick strokes.

stub.description: Straight run out of a port before the first bend. Default 15.

bundle_lane_gap.description: Clear space between the strokes of two lanes in one parallel-edge bundle. Default 8.

self_loop_gap.description:
Depth step between two self-loops stacked on one node border. Default 10, also the
default of [`SelfLoopOptions::gap`].

edge_label_margin.description:
Extra layer gap beyond an edge label's own layer-axis extent, so the edge has room for
the label and its arrow marker. Default 24.

edge_label_stack_gap.description: Clear space between two edge labels stacked in one layer gap. Default 6.

reroute_node_gap.description:
Order-axis gap [`crate::reroute()`] uses instead of [`Spacing::node_gap`]. Default 46.

A reroute keeps the caller's coordinates and runs no compaction, so a compaction preset's
tight `node_gap` would leave it cramped.

isolated_gap.description:
Padding around each cell of the grid that holds edgeless nodes, and the gap between that
grid and the connected drawing above it. Default 46.

isolated_max_columns.description: Column cap for the isolated-node grid. Further nodes wrap into new rows. Default 24.

compound_padding.description:
Room between a compound's border and its children's drawing, on every side
([`crate::Node::parent`]). Default 20.

compound_header.description:
Extra room along a compound's top border, on top of [`Spacing::compound_padding`], for a
title. Default 0.

Routing.description:
How edges are routed: the style, bundling, and which borders and lanes the ends use.

The repair passes after the first routing pass are in [`RoutingTuning`].

style.description: How edges are drawn between their ports. Default [`RoutingStyle::Orthogonal`].

bundle_parallel.description:
Route parallel edges with the same endpoints as one edge, then split it into offset lanes.
Default `true`. When off, each is routed separately and they can scatter across corridors.

lane_gap.description:
Room reserved per riser in a layer gap. A gap where `k` edges change height is widened to
at least `(k + 1) * lane_gap`, so risers never merge into one thick line. Default 8.

port_sides.description:
How readily an edge end may attach to a border across the layout axis instead of the one
facing the edge's direction. See [`PortSides`]. [`crate::Node::port_sides`] overrides it
per node. Default [`PortSides::Any`], but [`LayoutOptions::layered_default`] and
[`LayoutOptions::process_map`] use [`PortSides::FacingPreferred`].

centre_ports.description:
Which nodes pack a border's ends around its middle. See [`PortCentring`]. Default
[`PortCentring::Round`].

RoutingStyle.description: How edges are drawn between their ports.

oneOf.description:
Orthogonal segments through gutter lanes, with ports on the border centre or spread along
it. The default.

Diagonal segments. Each port sits where the ray from the node centre toward the other end
crosses the border, and a straight port-to-port line is used wherever it clears every
node box. Long edges keep side ports only where they add no crossing.

PortSides.description:
How readily an edge end may attach to a perpendicular border (e.g., top or bottom in a
left-to-right drawing) instead of the border facing along the flow.

The router moves an end to a perpendicular border to save a bend, only when that adds no
crossing in the layer gap before the node. Set per drawing in [`crate::Routing::port_sides`]
and per node in [`Node::port_sides`]. Under [`crate::RoutingStyle::Diagonal`],
`FacingPreferred` behaves like `Any`, and ellipse ports are radial and follow neither.

oneOf.description: A perpendicular border whenever it is free of crossings. The default.
Always the facing border, even at the cost of a bend.

A perpendicular border only when it is free of crossings and the facing border would cost
a crossing or overfill its ports at the port gap. Otherwise the facing border.

[`PortSides::FacingPreferred`] for an edge between adjacent layers, [`PortSides::Any`] for
a longer one, which would otherwise jog at each end to reach its track.

PortCentring.description:
Which nodes have the edge ends on a border packed around its middle. Default
[`PortCentring::Round`].

Spreading ends at the port gap pushes the outer ones onto a circle's shoulders, where the stroke
meets the curve at a glancing angle. Centring packs them half a port gap apart around the
middle, and on a round node may move an end that turns anyway to the free top or bottom border.

oneOf.description: Every end keeps the port the router spread it to.
Ellipse nodes centre their borders' ends.
Every node centres its borders' ends. Only ellipses move ends round a corner.

MergeEdges.description:
Which fan-outs and fan-ins [`Routing::merge_edges`] draws on a shared trunk.

A merge is made only where it adds no crossing or bend and cuts through no node.
[`crate::Layout::junctions`] marks the branch points.

oneOf.description: Every edge keeps its own port and line.
Edges leaving one node share a trunk.
Edges reaching one node share a trunk.
Both forks and joins.

OrderOptions.description:
Crossing-minimisation heuristic and group lane budgets.

How hard the ordering phases work is in [`OrderTuning`].

heuristic.description: Which one-sided heuristic the sweeps sort by. See [`OrderHeuristic`].

group_lane_budget_percent.description:
Crossings the lane pass may add to put each group ([`crate::Node::group`]) in a band of
its own, as a percentage of the crossings ordering left, plus
[`OrderTuning::group_lane_budget_floor`]. Default 0.

A banding that costs nothing is always taken. For clear lanes, try 100 here, a floor of 8
and [`OrderOptions::group_lane_area_percent`] of 50.

group_lane_area_percent.description:
How much wider the order axis may get, in percent, when the group bands are stacked into
disjoint slots. Default 0, which leaves the bands where the coordinate phases put them.

The stack is compressed to fit this budget, letting wide bands overlap at their edges.

group_lanes.description:
Whether group lanes are a preference traded against the two budgets above
([`GroupLanes::Soft`], the default) or required swimlanes ([`GroupLanes::Strict`]).

OrderHeuristic.description:
Which one-sided heuristic a crossing-minimisation sweep sorts a layer by. Default
[`OrderHeuristic::Alternate`].

Both place a node by where its neighbours in the previous layer sit. They differ on outliers:
Neighbours at `{0, 1, 20}` give position 7 under the barycentre and 1 under the median.

oneOf.description:
Weighted mean of the neighbours' positions (Sugiyama et al.). Heavy edges pull harder, so
the main flow ends up straighter.

Weighted median of the neighbours' positions (Eades and Wormald 1994), which has the
better worst-case guarantee on one bilayer.
Barycentre on even sweeps, median on odd ones. The best-scoring sweep is kept.

GroupLanes.description: How the groups ([`crate::Node::group`]) of a layered drawing are drawn.

oneOf.description:
Bands of the order axis where affordable. A banding over either
[`OrderOptions::group_lane_budget_percent`] or [`OrderOptions::group_lane_area_percent`]
is not drawn.

placement.description: Which optimiser places the order axis. Default [`Placement::NetworkSimplex`].

branch_bands.description:
Keep each branch off the main path in a band of its own, so one branch never slides into
a sibling's row. Default `true`. Graphs without a main path (several flows, caller seeds,
group lanes) are unaffected.

terminal_centering.description:
Centre a first- or last-layer terminal on the weighted median of its neighbours, so it
sits over its main flow. Default `false`, `true` in [`LayoutOptions::process_map`].

branch_style.description:
How a fork/join block's branches are drawn. See [`BranchStyle`]. Default
[`BranchStyle::Free`], but [`LayoutOptions::layered_default`] and
[`LayoutOptions::process_map`] use [`BranchStyle::StraightMain`].

CrossPlacement.description:
Which optimiser places the order axis.

Both keep the crossing-minimised order and every gap in [`crate::Spacing`]. They differ in
what they optimise within those constraints. [`CoordOptions`] defaults to
[`Placement::NetworkSimplex`].

oneOf.description:
Brandes-Kopf, as in dagre and ELK, followed by the straightness snap
([`CoordTuning::snap_rounds`]). Fast and local.

The dot placement (Gansner et al. 1993, section 4.2): A network simplex minimises the
total weighted cross-axis edge offset. Shorter edges and smaller area than Brandes-Kopf,
with more bends. Large graphs fall back to Brandes-Kopf
([`CoordTuning::simplex_max_nodes`]).

BranchStyle.description:
How the two branches of a fork/join block are drawn against each other.

[`crate::metrics::LayoutMetrics::split_alignment`] measures how many blocks come out aligned.

oneOf.description:
Keeps whatever placement produced. Suits graphs not read as blocks, such as dense
hub-and-spoke graphs.

One branch of each block runs straight from fork to join and the others are pushed aside
as skips. The straight branch is the heaviest, with ties going to the larger first node
along the layout axis.

The two branches sit at equal distance either side of the straight fork-join line. Only
possible when both branches start in the same layer. Adds crossings, so no preset uses it.

CompactionOptions.description: Cross-axis compaction. Its iteration counts are in [`CompactionTuning`].

mode.description: Whether the cross axis is compacted after placement.

Compaction.description: Whether the cross axis is compacted after placement. Default [`Compaction::None`].

oneOf.description: Leave the coordinates the placement passes produced.

Order-preserving priority compaction: Pack each layer, align it to its weighted-median
edges, then slide nodes toward their neighbours. Suits dense hub-and-spoke graphs.

SelfLoopOptions.description:
How self-loops (`source == target` edges) are drawn.

Self-loops take no part in cycle breaking, layering or ordering. Their room is reserved before
coordinate assignment, so placement widens exactly the slot the loops need.

side.description: Which border the loops bump out of. Default [`LoopSide::Auto`].

size.description:
How far the innermost loop reaches beyond the node's border. Default 15, the
[`Spacing::stub`] default, so a loop leaves its port by the same run as an ordinary edge.

gap.description:
Depth step between two loops stacked on one node, so `k` loops nest. Default 10, the
[`Spacing::self_loop_gap`] default.

label_gap.description: Clear space between the outer run of a loop and its own label box. Default 4.

LoopSide.description:
Which border of its node a self-loop bumps out of. Default [`LoopSide::Auto`].

The names are in flow terms, like [`crate::Margins`], so they hold for either [`Direction`].
`cross` is the order axis (along which one layer's nodes spread) and `along` the layer axis.

oneOf.description:
The positive order side (screen bottom in `LeftRight`, screen right in `TopBottom`). This
is the side [`crate::Margins::cross_pos`] reserves room on.
The negative order side.

The forward layer side, toward the next layer (screen right in `LeftRight`, screen bottom
in `TopBottom`).

Let the engine pick per node, once the layers are ordered.

A node with an order-axis neighbour on one side only uses the free side. Otherwise it uses
[`LoopSide::CrossPositive`], unless the node's own [`crate::Margins`] reserve more room on
the negative side.
