Glyph.description: The shape one counted glyph takes.

oneOf.description: Filled circle of the cluster's radius.
Rounded square inscribed in the cluster's diameter.

scale.description: Side length as a fraction of the diameter.

corner_radius.description: Corner radius of the square.

oneOf.description: A [`SymbolDef`] drawn in the cluster's box.

Separator.description:
A separator glyph drawn in the gap before a cluster, binding it to the cluster before it.
The bound pair is never split across rows.

symbol.description: Id of a [`SymbolDef`]. See [`crate::svg::builtin_symbols`] for the builtin ones.

width.description: Width of the box the symbol is drawn in.

height.description: Height of that box. It is centred on the row.

gap_before.description:
Space between the previous cluster and the separator. Together with
[`Separator::width`] and [`Separator::gap_after`] it takes the place of
[`ExactLayout::cluster_gap`] before this cluster.

gap_after.description: Space between the separator and this cluster.

color.description: Tint for the symbol. Falls back to the theme's arc colour.

oneOf.description: Glyphs at their clusters' own radius and step, wrapped into rows. The default.

Every glyph at one size chosen to fit the width. The clusters' radius and step are
ignored.

ExactLayout.description: Fixed-size clusters packed left to right, wrapping into further rows.

wrap_width.description:
Rows wrap once they would grow past this width. A single cluster wider than this still
gets a row of its own. Unbounded by default, `null` in JSON.

cluster_gap.description: Space between two neighbouring clusters (unless the second has a [`Separator`]).

row_gap.description: Space between two rows, on top of the largest glyph diameter.

max_bottom.description:
When several rows would run past this y, they are packed tighter (down to touching)
instead of overflowing, so no badge is dropped.

NumeralStyle.description: Style of the numeral a [`GlyphLayout::Fit`] row collapses to when it cannot fit.

size.description: Font size of the numeral.

weight.description: CSS numeric font weight of the numeral.

color.description: Fill colour. Falls back to the theme's text colour.

counted.description:
One line per non-empty cluster, its glyph followed by a multiplication sign (U+00D7) and
the count, instead of a single total. The lines shrink together to fit `max_width`.

FitLayout.description:
One row scaled to fit `max_width`, collapsing to a numeral when even the smallest glyphs
would not fit.

max_width.description: Width the row is scaled to fit. Unbounded by default, `null` in JSON.

gap.description: Edge-to-edge gap between glyphs.

min_diameter.description: Smallest glyph diameter. A row that would need smaller glyphs collapses to the numeral.

max_diameter.description: Largest glyph diameter, however much room the row has.

max_glyphs.description:
Most glyphs drawn one by one. A row with more collapses to the numeral even when they
would fit. Has no effect without a `numeral`.

numeral.description: `None` draws the glyphs at `min_diameter` and lets the row overflow instead of collapsing.

GlyphRow.description:
A counted-glyph row drawn inside a node: multiplicities, cardinalities, tokens, capacity
markers. Clusters run left to right, centred on the row's anchor.

dx.description: Horizontal offset of the row's centre from the node centre.

dy.description: Vertical offset of the row's first line from the node centre.

layout.description: How the clusters are sized and arranged.

attrs.description: When non-empty, the row is wrapped in a `<g>` carrying these attributes.

Ring.description:
A concentric ring drawn just inside a node's border. `inset` is the distance from the border
to the ring's outer edge. Rings follow the node's own shape.

color.description: Stroke colour.

inset.description:
Distance from the node's border inwards to the ring's outer edge. A ring with no room left
inside the node is not drawn.

SceneEdge.description: One edge: an already-routed polyline plus its styling, markers, labels and decorations.

points.description: The polyline in scene coordinates, source first. Fewer than two points draws nothing.

stroke.description:
How the path is stroked. A builtin marker without a colour of its own takes the stroke's
colour, or the theme's arc colour when the stroke is a gradient.

corner_radius.description: Radius the interior joins are rounded with. 0 draws straight segments.

hop_radius.description:
Radius of the semicircle a horizontal run of this edge draws where it crosses another
edge's vertical run. 0 draws crossings flat. Only crossings well inside both runs hop, so
a T junction or a crossing near a corner stays flat.

simplify.description:
Ramer-Douglas-Peucker tolerance applied to the *drawn* path only (0 = draw as given).
Labels and decorations still anchor on the points as passed in.

marker_start.description:
Marker at the first point. The drawn path is pulled back by the marker's tip gap so the
tip lands on the endpoint. See [`MarkerDef::tip_gap`]. Builtin markers compute their own.

marker_end.description: Marker at the last point, with the same pull-back.

labels.description: Text labels, drawn over the path and its decorations.

decorations.description: Dots, ticks, glyphs and bands along the edge. See [`Decoration`] for the paint order.

attrs.description: When non-empty, the edge is wrapped in a `<g>` carrying these attributes.

MarkerRef.description: Which marker an edge end uses.

oneOf.description: No marker.
One of the renderer's own markers, emitted once per distinct marker, colour and size.

color.description: Marker fill. Falls back to the edge's own stroke colour.

size.description: Side of the marker's 12-unit box in scene units. `None` scales with the stroke width.

oneOf.description: A [`MarkerDef`] by id.

BuiltinMarker.description:
The marker glyphs the renderer can draw without a user definition.

`Arrow`, `ArrowCentered`, `Ball` and `Bar` are the basic shapes. The four composites combine
them and could equally be written as a user [`MarkerDef`].

oneOf.description: Arrowhead anchored at its back, so the tip lands on the path's endpoint.
Arrowhead anchored at its centre, half-embedded past the endpoint.
Filled circle centred on the endpoint.
Perpendicular bar centred on the endpoint.
Arrowhead whose tip sits at a ball centred on the endpoint.
`ArrowCentered` with a perpendicular bar behind the tail.
Ball on the endpoint plus an arrowhead pointing back along the path.
`BallArrow` with a bar behind the arrow's tail.

EdgeLabel.description: A text label riding on an edge.

text.description: The text, anchored at [`EdgeLabel::at`] and then offset by its own `dx`/`dy`.

at.description: Where along the edge the label is anchored. Defaults to the middle of the polyline.

chip.description: A background chip. For a glyph-hugging outline instead, set [`TextRun::halo`].

attrs.description: When non-empty, the chip and text are wrapped in a `<g>` carrying these attributes.

EdgeAnchor.description: Where along an edge something is anchored.

anyOf.description:
A fraction (0..1) of the edge's length, along the line as drawn, so on its rounded
corners too.
An explicit point in scene coordinates.

`fraction` of the edge's length, then `offset` scene units further along the line
(negative towards its start), stopping at its ends.

fraction.description: A fraction (0..1) of the edge's length.

offset.description: Distance along the line from there.

Chip.description: A filled box drawn behind an edge label.

fill.description: Fill colour. Defaults to white.

padding.description: Space between the measured text box and the chip's border, on every side.

corner_radius.description: Corner radius of the chip.

Decoration.description:
Something drawn along an edge. `Band`s are painted under the edge's own path, in list order.
Everything else is painted over it.

oneOf.description: A circle centred on the anchor.

at.description: Where along the edge.

fill.description: Fill colour. Falls back to the theme's arc colour.

oneOf.description: A bar perpendicular to the path.

at.description: Where along the edge. The bar is perpendicular to the path's direction there.

length.description: Length of the bar, centred on the anchor.

slant.description:
Degrees the bar is turned from the perpendicular, towards the direction of travel at
its right-hand end. `0` crosses the path at a right angle.

oneOf.description: A [`SymbolDef`] centred on the anchor.

at.description: Where along the edge.

size.description: Size of the box the symbol is drawn in. The symbol is not rotated with the path.

color.description: Tint, set as `color` on the `<use>`. `None` inherits.

oneOf.description: A lane riding beside (or under) the edge, traced from its own already-routed points.

points.description: The band's own polyline, in scene coordinates. Fewer than two points draws nothing.

corner_radius.description: Radius its interior joins are rounded with. `0` draws straight segments.

Overlay.description: A fragment or panel drawn outside the node/edge stack.

z.description: Whether the overlay is drawn under or over the graph.

attrs.description: When non-empty, the overlay is wrapped in a `<g>` carrying these attributes.

ZOrder.description: Whether an overlay is drawn under or over the graph.

oneOf.description: Under the nodes and edges, over the background.
Over the nodes and edges.
Caller markup.
A legend panel, stacked by the renderer.

PanelSection.description: A titled group of legend entries.

title.description: Heading line drawn above the entries. `None` draws none.

attrs.description: When non-empty, the section is wrapped in a `<g>` carrying these attributes.

swatch.description: What is drawn left of the text.

swatch_advance.description:
Horizontal space reserved for the swatch before the text. `None` uses
[`PanelStyle::swatch_column`].

attrs.description: When non-empty, the entry is wrapped in a `<g>` carrying these attributes.

Swatch.description: The swatch drawn left of a [`LegendItem`]'s text.

oneOf.description: No swatch. The text starts at the item's text column anyway.
A plain rounded square in this colour.

color.description: The colour.

oneOf.description: A [`SymbolDef`], drawn in a box of `size` and tinted with `color` via `currentColor`.

size.description: Size of the symbol's box.

color.description: Tint. Falls back to the theme's arc colour.

oneOf.description: Caller markup, in scene coordinates.

PanelStyle.description: Sizes and colours a [`Panel`] stacks with.

title_size.description: Font size of a section title.

title_weight.description: CSS numeric font weight of a section title.

item_size.description: Font size of an entry. Entries are always drawn at weight 400.

line_height.description: Baseline-to-baseline distance between entries (and after a title).

swatch_column.description: Default horizontal space reserved for a swatch.

swatch_height.description: Height of the swatch box. It is centred on the entry's text.

swatch_dy.description: Offset of the swatch box's centre from the entry's baseline (negative = above it).

text_color.description: Colour of titles and entry text. Falls back to the theme's text colour.

Panel.description: A block of legend entries, stacked top-down from `origin`.

origin.description: Top-left of the panel. The first baseline sits at `origin.y`.

style.description: Sizes and colours.

attrs.description: When non-empty, the panel is wrapped in a `<g>` carrying these attributes.

DrawOrder.description: Whether edges are painted before or after nodes.

oneOf.description: Edges first, so the nodes cover any part of an edge that reaches into them.
Nodes first, so markers centred on a node border sit on top of it.

FontSpec.description: The font a text run is measured and drawn with.

family.description: CSS `font-family` list. Defaults to `Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif`.

size.description: Font size in scene units. Defaults to `12.5`.

weight.description: CSS numeric font weight (`400` regular, `700` bold). Defaults to `400`.

italic.description:
Italic style, passed to the [`crate::svg::TextMeasurer`] and drawn with
`font-style="italic"`.

name: oc_declare_svg
docs: Draw the model as a standalone SVG document.

OCDeclareArc.description: OC-DECLARE Constraint arc/edge between two nodes (i.e., activities)

label.description: Arc label specifying object involvement criteria

counts.description: First tuple element: min count (optional), Second: max count (optional)

OCDeclareArcType.description:
OC-DECLARE Arc Direction/Type

Models temporal relationships

oneOf.description: Association: No temporal restrictions
Eventually-Follows: Target must occur after source event
Eventually-Precedes: Target must occur before source event
Directly-Follows: Target must occur directly after source event (considering events that involve all required objects)
Directly-Precedes: Target must occur directly before source event (considering events that involve all required objects)

OCDeclareArcLabel.description: Object Involvement Label of an OC-DECLARE arc

each.description: Each (for each object of that type separately, there must be the specified number of relevant target events)

any.description: Any (there must be the specified number of relevant target events involving at least one of the objects of this type involved in the source event)

all.description: All (there must be the specified number of relevant target events involving all of the objects of this type involved in the source event)

ObjectTypeAssociation.description: Object Type Association: Direct or O2O Object Types

oneOf.description: Simple: Direct Object Types involved with an Activity
Indirect: Object Association through an O2O relationship

reversed.description:
Specifies the direction of the O2O relationship.

If reversed is `False`, `(first,second)` is considered

args.title: OCDeclareBuildOptions
args.description:
How a slice of [`OCDeclareArc`]s is turned into a [`Graph`]. Missing fields take the values of
[`OCDeclareBuildOptions::new`].

direction.description: Flow direction. `None` is the model's own default.

layout_patch.description:
Fields of the engine options to change, as a partial
[`LayoutOptions`](graphlay::LayoutOptions) object deep-merged over the model's preset and
the direction, e.g., `{"routing": {"style": "diagonal"}}`. `null` changes nothing.

fit_node_width.description: Widen each activity box to fit its label.

reverse_backward_arcs.description: Rank EP and DP arcs backwards, so the drawing reads forwards in time.

merge_mirrored_arcs.description:
Merge an EF (DF) arc and an EP (DP) arc mirroring it with the same object types into one
edge, which shows the EF (DF) arc's count bounds.

labels.description: How the arcs show their object types.

involvements.description:
Per activity, how many objects of each type one of its events involves, shown under its
name.

extra_activities.description:
Activities that become nodes even if no arc connects them, e.g., one just added in an
editor.

oneOf.description: Layers advance left to right.
Layers advance top to bottom.

LayoutOptions.description: Everything that steers one layout run.

direction.description: Which way the layers advance.

routing.description: Routing style, bundling and port choices.

coords.description: Cross-axis placement behaviour.

compaction.description: Whether and how the cross axis is compacted afterwards.

self_loops.description: How self-loops are placed and drawn.

labels.description: How edge labels are given room, and where they end up.

effort.description: How hard the engine works, as one dial. See [`Effort`].

seed.description:
Seed for the crossing minimisation's restarts and kicks. The same seed gives the same
drawing. 32 bits so it survives JSON in JavaScript. Default [`DEFAULT_SEED`].

limits.description: Input size limits. Exceeding one is an error instead of unbounded time.

wrap.description: Wrapping a long drawing into rows. Off unless a viewport shape is given.

cycles.description: Which edges of a cyclic graph are drawn against the flow.

seed_mode.description: How node positions given as seeds steer the layout.

tuning.description: The engine's internal iteration counts, budgets and thresholds. See [`Tuning`].

Spacing.description: Gaps and clearances, all in px.

layer_gap.description:
Between layer columns, on the layer axis. Default 54.

A left-to-right drawing's width grows with `n_layers * (node_w + layer_gap)`, so lower
this to narrow it.

node_gap.description: Between two real nodes in one layer, on the order axis. Default 46.

dummy_gap.description:
Between a routing track and its order-axis neighbour. Default 30, tighter than `node_gap`
because a track is a line.

port_gap.description: Minimum port-to-port separation along one border. Default 18.

port_stroke_clear.description:
Clear space between the strokes of two adjacent ports, on top of half of each stroke's
width. Default 14. Raise it for thick strokes.

stub.description: Straight run out of a port before the first bend. Default 15.

bundle_lane_gap.description: Clear space between the strokes of two lanes in one parallel-edge bundle. Default 8.

self_loop_gap.description:
Depth step between two self-loops stacked on one node border. Default 10, also the
default of [`SelfLoopOptions::gap`].

edge_label_margin.description:
Extra layer gap beyond an edge label's own layer-axis extent, so the edge has room for
the label and its arrow marker. Default 24.

edge_label_stack_gap.description: Clear space between two edge labels stacked in one layer gap. Default 6.

reroute_node_gap.description:
Order-axis gap [`crate::reroute()`] uses instead of [`Spacing::node_gap`]. Default 46.

A reroute keeps the caller's coordinates and runs no compaction, so a compaction preset's
tight `node_gap` would leave it cramped.

isolated_gap.description:
Padding around each cell of the grid that holds edgeless nodes, and the gap between that
grid and the connected drawing above it. Default 46.

isolated_max_columns.description: Column cap for the isolated-node grid. Further nodes wrap into new rows. Default 24.

compound_padding.description:
Room between a compound's border and its children's drawing, on every side
([`crate::Node::parent`]). Default 20.

compound_header.description:
Extra room along a compound's top border, on top of [`Spacing::compound_padding`], for a
title. Default 0.

Routing.description:
How edges are routed: the style, bundling, and which borders and lanes the ends use.

The repair passes after the first routing pass are in [`RoutingTuning`].

style.description: How edges are drawn between their ports. Default [`RoutingStyle::Orthogonal`].

bundle_parallel.description:
Route parallel edges with the same endpoints as one edge, then split it into offset lanes.
Default `true`. When off, each is routed separately and they can scatter across corridors.

lane_gap.description:
Room reserved per riser in a layer gap. A gap where `k` edges change height is widened to
at least `(k + 1) * lane_gap`, so risers never merge into one thick line. Default 8.

port_sides.description:
How readily an edge end may attach to a border across the layout axis instead of the one
facing the edge's direction. See [`PortSides`]. [`crate::Node::port_sides`] overrides it
per node. Default [`PortSides::Any`], but [`LayoutOptions::layered_default`] and
[`LayoutOptions::process_map`] use [`PortSides::FacingPreferred`].

centre_ports.description:
Which nodes pack a border's ends around its middle. See [`PortCentring`]. Default
[`PortCentring::Round`].

RoutingStyle.description: How edges are drawn between their ports.

oneOf.description:
Orthogonal segments through gutter lanes, with ports on the border centre or spread along
it. The default.

Diagonal segments. Each port sits where the ray from the node centre toward the other end
crosses the border, and a straight port-to-port line is used wherever it clears every
node box. Long edges keep side ports only where they add no crossing.

PortSides.description:
How readily an edge end may attach to a perpendicular border (e.g., top or bottom in a
left-to-right drawing) instead of the border facing along the flow.

The router moves an end to a perpendicular border to save a bend, only when that adds no
crossing in the layer gap before the node. Set per drawing in [`crate::Routing::port_sides`]
and per node in [`Node::port_sides`]. Under [`crate::RoutingStyle::Diagonal`],
`FacingPreferred` behaves like `Any`, and ellipse ports are radial and follow neither.

oneOf.description: A perpendicular border whenever it is free of crossings. The default.
Always the facing border, even at the cost of a bend.

A perpendicular border only when it is free of crossings and the facing border would cost
a crossing or overfill its ports at the port gap. Otherwise the facing border.

[`PortSides::FacingPreferred`] for an edge between adjacent layers, [`PortSides::Any`] for
a longer one, which would otherwise jog at each end to reach its track.

PortCentring.description:
Which nodes have the edge ends on a border packed around its middle. Default
[`PortCentring::Round`].

Spreading ends at the port gap pushes the outer ones onto a circle's shoulders, where the stroke
meets the curve at a glancing angle. Centring packs them half a port gap apart around the
middle, and on a round node may move an end that turns anyway to the free top or bottom border.

oneOf.description: Every end keeps the port the router spread it to.
Ellipse nodes centre their borders' ends.
Every node centres its borders' ends. Only ellipses move ends round a corner.

MergeEdges.description:
Which fan-outs and fan-ins [`Routing::merge_edges`] draws on a shared trunk.

A merge is made only where it adds no crossing or bend and cuts through no node.
[`crate::Layout::junctions`] marks the branch points.

oneOf.description: Every edge keeps its own port and line.
Edges leaving one node share a trunk.
Edges reaching one node share a trunk.
Both forks and joins.

OrderOptions.description:
Crossing-minimisation heuristic and group lane budgets.

How hard the ordering phases work is in [`OrderTuning`].

heuristic.description: Which one-sided heuristic the sweeps sort by. See [`OrderHeuristic`].

group_lane_budget_percent.description:
Crossings the lane pass may add to put each group ([`crate::Node::group`]) in a band of
its own, as a percentage of the crossings ordering left, plus
[`OrderTuning::group_lane_budget_floor`]. Default 0.

A banding that costs nothing is always taken. For clear lanes, try 100 here, a floor of 8
and [`OrderOptions::group_lane_area_percent`] of 50.

group_lane_area_percent.description:
How much wider the order axis may get, in percent, when the group bands are stacked into
disjoint slots. Default 0, which leaves the bands where the coordinate phases put them.

The stack is compressed to fit this budget, letting wide bands overlap at their edges.

group_lanes.description:
Whether group lanes are a preference traded against the two budgets above
([`GroupLanes::Soft`], the default) or required swimlanes ([`GroupLanes::Strict`]).

OrderHeuristic.description:
Which one-sided heuristic a crossing-minimisation sweep sorts a layer by. Default
[`OrderHeuristic::Alternate`].

Both place a node by where its neighbours in the previous layer sit. They differ on outliers:
Neighbours at `{0, 1, 20}` give position 7 under the barycentre and 1 under the median.

oneOf.description:
Weighted mean of the neighbours' positions (Sugiyama et al.). Heavy edges pull harder, so
the main flow ends up straighter.

Weighted median of the neighbours' positions (Eades and Wormald 1994), which has the
better worst-case guarantee on one bilayer.
Barycentre on even sweeps, median on odd ones. The best-scoring sweep is kept.

GroupLanes.description: How the groups ([`crate::Node::group`]) of a layered drawing are drawn.

oneOf.description:
Bands of the order axis where affordable. A banding over either
[`OrderOptions::group_lane_budget_percent`] or [`OrderOptions::group_lane_area_percent`]
is not drawn.

placement.description: Which optimiser places the order axis. Default [`Placement::NetworkSimplex`].

branch_bands.description:
Keep each branch off the main path in a band of its own, so one branch never slides into
a sibling's row. Default `true`. Graphs without a main path (several flows, caller seeds,
group lanes) are unaffected.

terminal_centering.description:
Centre a first- or last-layer terminal on the weighted median of its neighbours, so it
sits over its main flow. Default `false`, `true` in [`LayoutOptions::process_map`].

branch_style.description:
How a fork/join block's branches are drawn. See [`BranchStyle`]. Default
[`BranchStyle::Free`], but [`LayoutOptions::layered_default`] and
[`LayoutOptions::process_map`] use [`BranchStyle::StraightMain`].

CrossPlacement.description:
Which optimiser places the order axis.

Both keep the crossing-minimised order and every gap in [`crate::Spacing`]. They differ in
what they optimise within those constraints. [`CoordOptions`] defaults to
[`Placement::NetworkSimplex`].

oneOf.description:
Brandes-Kopf, as in dagre and ELK, followed by the straightness snap
([`CoordTuning::snap_rounds`]). Fast and local.

The dot placement (Gansner et al. 1993, section 4.2): A network simplex minimises the
total weighted cross-axis edge offset. Shorter edges and smaller area than Brandes-Kopf,
with more bends. Large graphs fall back to Brandes-Kopf
([`CoordTuning::simplex_max_nodes`]).

BranchStyle.description:
How the two branches of a fork/join block are drawn against each other.

[`crate::metrics::LayoutMetrics::split_alignment`] measures how many blocks come out aligned.

oneOf.description:
Keeps whatever placement produced. Suits graphs not read as blocks, such as dense
hub-and-spoke graphs.

One branch of each block runs straight from fork to join and the others are pushed aside
as skips. The straight branch is the heaviest, with ties going to the larger first node
along the layout axis.

The two branches sit at equal distance either side of the straight fork-join line. Only
possible when both branches start in the same layer. Adds crossings, so no preset uses it.

CompactionOptions.description: Cross-axis compaction. Its iteration counts are in [`CompactionTuning`].

mode.description: Whether the cross axis is compacted after placement.

Compaction.description: Whether the cross axis is compacted after placement. Default [`Compaction::None`].

oneOf.description: Leave the coordinates the placement passes produced.

Order-preserving priority compaction: Pack each layer, align it to its weighted-median
edges, then slide nodes toward their neighbours. Suits dense hub-and-spoke graphs.

SelfLoopOptions.description:
How self-loops (`source == target` edges) are drawn.

Self-loops take no part in cycle breaking, layering or ordering. Their room is reserved before
coordinate assignment, so placement widens exactly the slot the loops need.

side.description: Which border the loops bump out of. Default [`LoopSide::Auto`].

size.description:
How far the innermost loop reaches beyond the node's border. Default 15, the
[`Spacing::stub`] default, so a loop leaves its port by the same run as an ordinary edge.

gap.description:
Depth step between two loops stacked on one node, so `k` loops nest. Default 10, the
[`Spacing::self_loop_gap`] default.

label_gap.description: Clear space between the outer run of a loop and its own label box. Default 4.

LoopSide.description:
Which border of its node a self-loop bumps out of. Default [`LoopSide::Auto`].

The names are in flow terms, like [`crate::Margins`], so they hold for either [`Direction`].
`cross` is the order axis (along which one layer's nodes spread) and `along` the layer axis.

oneOf.description:
The positive order side (screen bottom in `LeftRight`, screen right in `TopBottom`). This
is the side [`crate::Margins::cross_pos`] reserves room on.
The negative order side.

The forward layer side, toward the next layer (screen right in `LeftRight`, screen bottom
in `TopBottom`).

Let the engine pick per node, once the layers are ordered.

A node with an order-axis neighbour on one side only uses the free side. Otherwise it uses
[`LoopSide::CrossPositive`], unless the node's own [`crate::Margins`] reserve more room on
the negative side.

LabelOptions.description: How edge labels are given room, and where in the drawing they end up.

reservation.description: When a layer gap is widened to hold a label.

placement.description: How the final position is chosen.

clearance.description:
Clear space a label tries to keep from node boxes, other labels and other edges. Soft: A
position with less clearance is penalised for the shortfall. Default 4.

LabelReservation.description:
When a layer gap is widened to hold the labels crossing it. Default
[`LabelReservation::WhenNeeded`].

Reservation is the only guarantee of room, and it costs width because every label widens its
gap.

oneOf.description: Every labelled edge widens its gap to hold its label.

Only a label too large for the order-axis space between two nodes of a layer
([`Spacing::node_gap`]) widens its gap. Smaller ones are left to
[`LabelPlacement::Candidates`], which can put them in that space. The test uses the label's
extent across the flow.

Nothing is reserved. Placement fits each label into whatever free space exists, and
takes the least-bad position when there is none.

LabelPlacement.description: How a label's final position is chosen. Default [`LabelPlacement::Candidates`].

oneOf.description: The middle of its reserved gap, with labels sharing a gap stacked across the flow.

The best of several positions along the edge's own polyline (near the source, middle or
target, on either side of the line), scored by what each one overlaps.

Effort.description:
How hard the engine works, as one dial over the iteration counts. Default
[`Effort::Balanced`].

`Balanced` leaves [`OrderTuning`] and [`CoordTuning`] as given, so hand-tuned counts survive.
Any other value overwrites the counts in its [`Effort::budget`]. `Thorough` usually saves a
few crossings on dense graphs for two to three times the time.

oneOf.description: Fewer restarts and sweeps, for interactive relayout of large graphs.
The [`Tuning`] counts as given.
More restarts and sweeps, for a final rendering.
Exactly these counts.

EffortBudget.description: The iteration counts one [`Effort`] resolves to.

exhaustive_layer_max.description: Brute-force permutation cap ([`OrderTuning::exhaustive_layer_max`]).

sifting_rounds.description: Sifting rounds per wide layer ([`OrderTuning::sifting_rounds`]).

pullin_rounds.description: Channel pull-in rounds, applied only when [`CoordTuning::pullin_rounds`] is non-zero.

kick_patience.description:
Rejected kicks per layer before the local search gives up on it
([`OrderTuning::kick_patience`]).

Limits.description:
Input size limits.

All `None` by default. Set them when the input is untrusted (e.g., JSON from a wasm caller).
Exceeding a limit is [`LayoutError::TooLarge`], never a hang or a panic.

max_dummies.description:
Largest accepted routing-waypoint count (one per layer a long edge passes), checked after
layering. [`crate::LayoutError::TooLarge`] names it `"routing waypoints"`.

WrapOptions.description:
Wrapping a long drawing into rows to fit a viewport shape. When a wrap pays is in
[`WrapTuning`].

viewport_aspect.description: Width over height of the viewport the drawing is shown in. Default `0`, never wrap.

strategy.description: Which edges of a cycle are drawn backwards.

CycleStrategy.description:
Which edges of a cyclic graph are drawn against the flow. Default
[`CycleStrategy::MinimumReversal`].

A layered drawing draws one edge per cycle backwards.

oneOf.description:
Reverse as little edge weight as possible (a heuristic minimum feedback arc set). Fewest
crossings, but a rare step can be drawn before the steps that lead to it.

Order the nodes inside a cycle by distance from where the flow enters it, so every
reversed edge reads as a return to an earlier point. Can cost crossings on dense graphs.

SeedMode.description:
How node positions given by the caller ([`crate::Node::position`]) steer a layout. Default
[`SeedMode::Placement`].

oneOf.description:
Seeds set the nodes' cross-axis positions, but layering and ordering run from scratch.
A changed graph can land in other layers and orders, so the drawing may jump.

Tuning.description:
Iteration counts, budgets and thresholds, tuned on the fixture corpus.

A non-`Balanced` [`LayoutOptions::effort`] overrides the ordering counts in [`OrderTuning`]
and [`CoordTuning::pullin_rounds`].

routing.description: The router's repair passes.

coords.description: The coordinate phases' rounds and budgets.

compaction.description: Priority compaction's rounds.

labels.description: Label placement's candidates and rounds.

wrap.description: When and how far a drawing is wrapped.

diagonal_clear.description:
Minimum clearance between a diagonal segment and a node box. A closer segment takes a
corner detour, since a graze reads as badly as a hit. Default 8.

diagonal_detour_margin.description: How far outside a node box a diagonal's corner detour is placed. Default 12.

bundle_nest_gap.description:
How far past the inner channel's turn an outer channel is carried when two nested
long-edge channels would otherwise cross at their shared target. Default 12.

endpoint_snap.description: Largest port jog that is straightened onto the edge's main track. Default 6.

endpoint_snap_min_track.description: Shortest segment that counts as a main track. Default 25.

step_flatten.description:
Tallest step (run, perpendicular jog, run) merged away after routing by moving one run onto
the other's line. Default `1.0e6` (no cap), `0.0` disables the pass.

A move is taken only if it hits no node box, keeps ports [`Spacing::port_gap`] apart, and
adds no crossing or overlap.

port_relax_clear.description:
Minimum distance between two ports on adjacent borders of one node, the corner case
`port_gap` does not cover. Default 10.

port_relax_step.description: Step of the greedy nudge that enforces `port_relax_clear`. Default 3.

port_relax_rounds.description: Iterations of that nudge per node. Default 48.

overlap_repair_rounds.description:
Rounds of the repair that separates two edges' runs drawn on one line along the layer
axis, where that adds no box hit or crossing. Default 8. `0` disables it.

overlap_repair_step.description:
How far that repair moves a run or a port, in one or two steps. Default 8. `0.0`
disables the repair.

OrderTuning.description:
How hard the crossing-minimisation and lane phases work ([`Tuning::order`]).

The counts do not scale with graph size. A non-`Balanced` [`Effort`] overwrites the restart,
sweep, permutation, sifting and kick counts.

seeds.description:
Ordering restarts. Default 9. The first three are structural (a DFS seed, its mirror, and
a DFS from the last layer), the rest deterministic shuffles of the first.

sweeps.description:
Upper bound on forward and backward sweeps per restart. Default 8. A restart stops early
after [`OrderTuning::sweep_stall`] sweeps without improvement.

sweep_stall.description:
Consecutive non-improving sweeps after which a restart gives up. Default 2. `0` is read as
`1`.

exhaustive_layer_max.description: Layers with 2 to this many nodes are ordered by trying every permutation. Default 5.

sifting_min_layer.description:
Layers wider than this get the sifting pass. Default 2. The kicks only visit layers that
sift, so raising it also removes layers from the local search.

sifting_rounds.description:
Upper bound on sifting rounds over the layer stack. Default 8. A round sifts every layer
still moving and wakes the neighbours of those that moved. It stops early when a round
moves nothing.

sifting_max_work.description:
Work ceiling for sifting one layer, in arc pairs (about `e^2` for `e` arcs on its two
sides). A heavier layer is left to the sweeps. Default 160000.

sifting_sweep_max_arcs.description:
Arc count up to which sifting also runs inside each restart's sweeps, instead of only on
the winning order. It multiplies sifting cost by the restart count. Default 20000.

kick_rounds.description:
Upper bound on kicks the iterated local search tries on the winning order. A kick reverses
a short run of one layer, re-sifts, and is kept only if strictly better. Usually
[`OrderTuning::kick_patience`] stops the pass first. Default 30000. `0` disables it.

kick_patience.description:
Consecutive rejected kicks per layer after which that layer leaves the kick pool. An
accepted kick resets its layer and both neighbours. Default 64. `0` is read as `1`.

kick_max_span.description:
Longest run of a layer one kick may reverse. Each kick picks a length from 2 up to this.
Default 8.

group_relax_iters.description:
Relaxation iterations that spread lane values from grouped to ungrouped nodes.
Default 64.

group_sort_rounds.description: Re-sort rounds of the group lane pass. Default 8.

group_lane_budget_floor.description:
Crossings the lane pass may add on top of [`OrderOptions::group_lane_budget_percent`].
Default 0. A nearly planar drawing has no crossings to take a percentage of, so this
floor is what lets it get lanes.

group_lane_sweeps.description:
Barycentre sweeps over the banded order, each re-sorting every layer within its bands.
Default 4.

group_lane_repair_rounds.description:
Rounds of band-preserving adjacent swaps that win back crossings the banding cost.
Default 3.

group_lane_order_rounds.description: Rounds of adjacent band swaps looking for a band order with fewer crossings. Default 2.

chain_lane_rounds.description:
Rounds of the chain-lane pass, which moves a long edge's waypoints past their neighbours
where that costs no crossing and lets the edge run on one lane. Default 3. `0` disables the
pass.

chain_lane_size_threshold.description:
On a graph with more routing waypoints than this, the chain-lane pass skips chains longer
than [`OrderTuning::chain_lane_max_span`]. Default 2000.

chain_lane_max_span.description: Longest chain the chain-lane pass still works on above the size threshold. Default 12.

chain_lane_max_steps.description:
How many positions the chain-lane pass may move one waypoint in one go. A walk is kept
whole if it opens the lane, else undone. Default 5.

balance_rounds.description:
Rounds of the side-balancing pass, which mirrors branches off the main path to whichever
side evens out the layers, where that costs no crossing. Default 4. `0` disables it.

CoordTuning.description: Iteration counts and budgets of the coordinate phases ([`Tuning::coords`]).

simplex_max_nodes.description:
Auxiliary-graph size (layered nodes plus arcs) above which [`Placement::NetworkSimplex`]
falls back to Brandes-Kopf. Default 10000.

simplex_max_pivots.description:
Simplex iterations before [`Placement::NetworkSimplex`] stops with its best placement so
far. Every iteration is feasible, so a capped solve is still a valid drawing. Default
50000.

simplex_face_rounds.description:
Rounds of the walk over the simplex's optimal face that re-places each long edge, heaviest
first, on the fewest lanes possible at the same cost. Default 2. `0` switches it off.
Brandes-Kopf ignores it.

snap_rounds.description:
Rounds of the straightness snap after Brandes-Kopf. Default 8. The network simplex
ignores it.

main_path_room.description:
How much wider, in percent, the drawing may get to draw its heaviest source-to-sink path
as one straight line, but at least the widest node on the path. Default 15. `0` turns the
pass off.

balance_width_slack.description:
How much wider than the balanced placement one of Brandes-Kopf's four biased passes may
be and still be chosen, in percent. Default 20.

flatten_room.description:
Pixels of layer width one removed staircase step is worth when chain flattening pushes a
node aside to free a lane. Default 300. `0` turns the phase off.

pullin_rounds.description:
Rounds of channel pull-in, which moves a long edge's waypoints past a real node standing
between them and their endpoints' line when crossings allow. Default 0 (off), 3 in
[`LayoutOptions::process_map`].

branch_rounds.description:
Rounds of the [`BranchStyle`] pass. Each round walks every block innermost-first and
stops early once a round aligns nothing new. Default 3.

offset_rounds.description: Rounds of rigid per-layer offsetting. Default 24.

refine_rounds.description: Rounds of per-node refinement inside the packed envelope. Default 8.

LabelTuning.description: The candidate positions and rounds of label placement ([`Tuning::labels`]).

fractions.description:
Fractions along its own polyline at which a label is tried, besides the midpoint of the
longest segment. Ties go to the earlier fraction. Default `[0.5, 0.32, 0.68, 0.18, 0.82]`.

side_steps.description:
How far off its line a label may be pushed, as multiples of the distance that just clears
the line (half the label's extent across the line, plus the stroke, plus
[`LabelOptions::clearance`]). Both sides are tried, nearest first. Default `[1, 2, 4, 8]`.

rounds.description:
Rounds of placement. Round one ignores other labels, and each further round re-places
every label against the others. Default 2. `0` places nothing.

WrapTuning.description:
When and how far a drawing is wrapped once [`WrapOptions::viewport_aspect`] asks for it
([`Tuning::wrap`]).

max_rows.description: Most rows a drawing is wrapped into. Default 4.

min_gain.description:
Scale factor by which the drawing must grow in the viewport for a wrap to be taken.
Default 1.2. Every edge across a cut gets a U-turn, which a small gain does not pay for.

max_cut_edges.description: Most edges one cut may carry to the next row. Default 4.

OCDeclareLabels.description: How an arc shows its object types.

oneOf.description: A chip naming the types, e.g., `Each(orders), Any(items)`.
Discs on the line: one for each, three for all, one filled and two hollow for any.

ObjectInvolvementCounts.description: Stores statistics on the number of objects of a certain type involved with an activity or in an O2O relationship.

min.description: The minimum number of objects of a given type involved in a single instance.

max.description: The maximum number of objects of a given type involved in a single instance.

args.title: OCDeclareStyle
args.description: Colors and sizes of an OC-DECLARE drawing.

base.description: Colors and paddings shared with every other model.

plain_activities.description: Draw the activities in the base node colors instead of tinting each one.

fill_lightness.description: How far towards white an activity's color is washed for its fill.

marker.description: Color of the markers, and of an arc that names no object type.

BaseStyle.description: Colors, sizes and paddings shared by all model drawings.

background.description: Page background. `None` leaves the SVG transparent.

padding.description: Space kept around the drawing's bounding box, in px.

corner_radius.description: Corner radius of a box-shaped node.

Palette.description:
The six colours every drawable falls back to.

Pass the on-screen theme's resolved colours here so an export matches the screen.

node_bg.description: Node fill, where a node names none. Default `#ffffff`.

node_border.description: Node border, where a node names no stroke. Default `#1f2937`.

node_text.description: Text, token and numeral fill, where a run names no colour. Default `#111827`.

arc_color.description:
Fallback for edge dots, separators, symbol swatches and a builtin marker on a gradient
stroke. Default `#374151`.

arc_label_bg.description:
Background behind an edge label (its halo or chip), where the label names none. Default
`#ffffff`.

export_bg.description: Fill of a hollow edge dot. Default `#ffffff`.

name: oc_declare_svg_from_layout
docs: Draw the model over a layout of its graph as a standalone SVG document, so no [`Scene`]
crosses the binding boundary.

OCDeclareArc.description: OC-DECLARE Constraint arc/edge between two nodes (i.e., activities)

label.description: Arc label specifying object involvement criteria

counts.description: First tuple element: min count (optional), Second: max count (optional)

OCDeclareArcType.description:
OC-DECLARE Arc Direction/Type

Models temporal relationships

oneOf.description: Association: No temporal restrictions
Eventually-Follows: Target must occur after source event
Eventually-Precedes: Target must occur before source event
Directly-Follows: Target must occur directly after source event (considering events that involve all required objects)
Directly-Precedes: Target must occur directly before source event (considering events that involve all required objects)

OCDeclareArcLabel.description: Object Involvement Label of an OC-DECLARE arc

each.description: Each (for each object of that type separately, there must be the specified number of relevant target events)

any.description: Any (there must be the specified number of relevant target events involving at least one of the objects of this type involved in the source event)

all.description: All (there must be the specified number of relevant target events involving all of the objects of this type involved in the source event)

ObjectTypeAssociation.description: Object Type Association: Direct or O2O Object Types

oneOf.description: Simple: Direct Object Types involved with an Activity
Indirect: Object Association through an O2O relationship

reversed.description:
Specifies the direction of the O2O relationship.

If reversed is `False`, `(first,second)` is considered

args.title: Layout
args.description: One laid-out drawing.

nodes.description: One entry per input node, in [`crate::NodeId`] order.

edges.description: One entry per input edge, in [`crate::EdgeId`] order.

bounds.description: Bounding box of every node box, polyline point and label anchor, without padding.

layer_count.description:
Number of layers in a layered drawing, or of depth rows in a tidy tree. `0` for an empty
graph.

reversed.description:
Edges the layering saw the other way round: Those the cycle breaker reversed, plus those
with [`crate::Edge::reverse_for_ranking`] (an edge that is both is not listed). Their
polylines still run source to target.

junctions.description:
Where a merged edge branches off a shared trunk ([`crate::Routing::merge_edges`]), for a
renderer to mark with a dot. Empty unless edges were merged.

lanes.description:
The swimlanes of a drawing with [`crate::GroupLanes::Strict`] lanes, in order along the
order axis. Empty otherwise.

center.description: Centre of the node's box, in output space.

size.description: The node's size, echoed from the input so a renderer needs only the layout.

rank.description: Layer index. `None` for an edgeless node packed into the grid below the layered drawing.

order.description:
Position within the layer. Routing waypoints count too, so two nodes with a long edge's
track between them are two apart.

Point.description: A point in output (drawing) space, in px.

x.description: Horizontal coordinate, growing to the right.

Size.description: The full extent of an axis-aligned box, in px.

points.description:
Border-to-border polyline, source first. At least two points for a routed edge, four for
a [`RouteKind::SelfLoop`] and none for [`RouteKind::Unrouted`].

source_port.description: Where the polyline leaves the source node, or `None` when there is no polyline.

target_port.description: Where the polyline enters the target node, or `None` when there is no polyline.

kind.description: What kind of route this is.

label_anchor.description: Where to centre this edge's label, when [`crate::Edge::label_size`] is set.

PortInfo.description: How an edge attaches to one of its nodes.

point.description: The point on the node's border the polyline starts (or ends) at.

side.description:
Which border that is, in output space. For an end placed by a port hint
([`crate::Edge::source_port`] / [`crate::Edge::target_port`]), the hinted border.

offset.description:
Signed distance in px along the border from its middle to [`PortInfo::point`]. Positive
is down on the left and right borders and right on the top and bottom borders.

Side.description:
One border of a node's bounding box.

In [`crate::layout::PortInfo`] sides are in output space, so `Top` is the smaller-`y` border
whatever the [`crate::Direction`].

oneOf.description: The larger-`x` border.
The smaller-`x` border.
The smaller-`y` border.
The larger-`y` border.
A route between two adjacent layers, with no routing waypoints.
A long edge, routed through a chain of waypoints.

spans.description: How many layer gaps it crosses (always `> 1`).

oneOf.description:
An edge from a node to itself, drawn as a rounded bump out of one of its borders
([`crate::SelfLoopOptions`]). Loops on one node nest by edge order.

One lane of a bundle: several edges sharing a source and a target, routed once as a single
corridor and then spread into parallel lanes.

lane.description: Index of this edge's lane within its bundle, in edge order.

oneOf.description: No polyline of at least two points. The layered pipeline does not return it.

Rect.description:
An axis-aligned rectangle from its top-left `min` to its bottom-right `max`. The default is
the empty rectangle at the origin.

LayoutStats.description: Counters from the run that produced a [`Layout`].

dummy_count.description: Routing waypoints (dummy nodes) the long edges were cut into.

Lane.description: One swimlane: a strip across the whole drawing that holds one group's nodes.

group.description: The group the lane holds, or `None` for the lane of nodes without a group.

rect.description:
The lane's rectangle. Adjacent lanes share their border, halfway across the gap between
their nodes, and every lane spans the drawing's full extent along the layer axis.

GroupId.description:
A lane group. Nodes sharing one are drawn in a lane of their own.

Groups are opaque ids, only compared and ordered. Lanes appear only when nodes carry at least
two distinct groups (see [`Node::group`]).

args.title: OCDeclareBuildOptions
args.description:
How a slice of [`OCDeclareArc`]s is turned into a [`Graph`]. Missing fields take the values of
[`OCDeclareBuildOptions::new`].

direction.description: Flow direction. `None` is the model's own default.

layout_patch.description:
Fields of the engine options to change, as a partial
[`LayoutOptions`](graphlay::LayoutOptions) object deep-merged over the model's preset and
the direction, e.g., `{"routing": {"style": "diagonal"}}`. `null` changes nothing.

fit_node_width.description: Widen each activity box to fit its label.

reverse_backward_arcs.description: Rank EP and DP arcs backwards, so the drawing reads forwards in time.

merge_mirrored_arcs.description:
Merge an EF (DF) arc and an EP (DP) arc mirroring it with the same object types into one
edge, which shows the EF (DF) arc's count bounds.

labels.description: How the arcs show their object types.

involvements.description:
Per activity, how many objects of each type one of its events involves, shown under its
name.

extra_activities.description:
Activities that become nodes even if no arc connects them, e.g., one just added in an
editor.

oneOf.description: Layers advance left to right.
Layers advance top to bottom.

LayoutOptions.description: Everything that steers one layout run.

direction.description: Which way the layers advance.

routing.description: Routing style, bundling and port choices.

coords.description: Cross-axis placement behaviour.

compaction.description: Whether and how the cross axis is compacted afterwards.

self_loops.description: How self-loops are placed and drawn.

labels.description: How edge labels are given room, and where they end up.

effort.description: How hard the engine works, as one dial. See [`Effort`].

seed.description:
Seed for the crossing minimisation's restarts and kicks. The same seed gives the same
drawing. 32 bits so it survives JSON in JavaScript. Default [`DEFAULT_SEED`].

limits.description: Input size limits. Exceeding one is an error instead of unbounded time.

wrap.description: Wrapping a long drawing into rows. Off unless a viewport shape is given.

cycles.description: Which edges of a cyclic graph are drawn against the flow.

seed_mode.description: How node positions given as seeds steer the layout.

tuning.description: The engine's internal iteration counts, budgets and thresholds. See [`Tuning`].

Spacing.description: Gaps and clearances, all in px.

layer_gap.description:
Between layer columns, on the layer axis. Default 54.

A left-to-right drawing's width grows with `n_layers * (node_w + layer_gap)`, so lower
this to narrow it.

node_gap.description: Between two real nodes in one layer, on the order axis. Default 46.

dummy_gap.description:
Between a routing track and its order-axis neighbour. Default 30, tighter than `node_gap`
because a track is a line.

port_gap.description: Minimum port-to-port separation along one border. Default 18.

port_stroke_clear.description:
Clear space between the strokes of two adjacent ports, on top of half of each stroke's
width. Default 14. Raise it for thick strokes.

stub.description: Straight run out of a port before the first bend. Default 15.

bundle_lane_gap.description: Clear space between the strokes of two lanes in one parallel-edge bundle. Default 8.

self_loop_gap.description:
Depth step between two self-loops stacked on one node border. Default 10, also the
default of [`SelfLoopOptions::gap`].

edge_label_margin.description:
Extra layer gap beyond an edge label's own layer-axis extent, so the edge has room for
the label and its arrow marker. Default 24.

edge_label_stack_gap.description: Clear space between two edge labels stacked in one layer gap. Default 6.

reroute_node_gap.description:
Order-axis gap [`crate::reroute()`] uses instead of [`Spacing::node_gap`]. Default 46.

A reroute keeps the caller's coordinates and runs no compaction, so a compaction preset's
tight `node_gap` would leave it cramped.

isolated_gap.description:
Padding around each cell of the grid that holds edgeless nodes, and the gap between that
grid and the connected drawing above it. Default 46.

isolated_max_columns.description: Column cap for the isolated-node grid. Further nodes wrap into new rows. Default 24.

compound_padding.description:
Room between a compound's border and its children's drawing, on every side
([`crate::Node::parent`]). Default 20.

compound_header.description:
Extra room along a compound's top border, on top of [`Spacing::compound_padding`], for a
title. Default 0.

Routing.description:
How edges are routed: the style, bundling, and which borders and lanes the ends use.

The repair passes after the first routing pass are in [`RoutingTuning`].

style.description: How edges are drawn between their ports. Default [`RoutingStyle::Orthogonal`].

bundle_parallel.description:
Route parallel edges with the same endpoints as one edge, then split it into offset lanes.
Default `true`. When off, each is routed separately and they can scatter across corridors.

lane_gap.description:
Room reserved per riser in a layer gap. A gap where `k` edges change height is widened to
at least `(k + 1) * lane_gap`, so risers never merge into one thick line. Default 8.

port_sides.description:
How readily an edge end may attach to a border across the layout axis instead of the one
facing the edge's direction. See [`PortSides`]. [`crate::Node::port_sides`] overrides it
per node. Default [`PortSides::Any`], but [`LayoutOptions::layered_default`] and
[`LayoutOptions::process_map`] use [`PortSides::FacingPreferred`].

centre_ports.description:
Which nodes pack a border's ends around its middle. See [`PortCentring`]. Default
[`PortCentring::Round`].

RoutingStyle.description: How edges are drawn between their ports.

oneOf.description:
Orthogonal segments through gutter lanes, with ports on the border centre or spread along
it. The default.

Diagonal segments. Each port sits where the ray from the node centre toward the other end
crosses the border, and a straight port-to-port line is used wherever it clears every
node box. Long edges keep side ports only where they add no crossing.

PortSides.description:
How readily an edge end may attach to a perpendicular border (e.g., top or bottom in a
left-to-right drawing) instead of the border facing along the flow.

The router moves an end to a perpendicular border to save a bend, only when that adds no
crossing in the layer gap before the node. Set per drawing in [`crate::Routing::port_sides`]
and per node in [`Node::port_sides`]. Under [`crate::RoutingStyle::Diagonal`],
`FacingPreferred` behaves like `Any`, and ellipse ports are radial and follow neither.

oneOf.description: A perpendicular border whenever it is free of crossings. The default.
Always the facing border, even at the cost of a bend.

A perpendicular border only when it is free of crossings and the facing border would cost
a crossing or overfill its ports at the port gap. Otherwise the facing border.

[`PortSides::FacingPreferred`] for an edge between adjacent layers, [`PortSides::Any`] for
a longer one, which would otherwise jog at each end to reach its track.

PortCentring.description:
Which nodes have the edge ends on a border packed around its middle. Default
[`PortCentring::Round`].

Spreading ends at the port gap pushes the outer ones onto a circle's shoulders, where the stroke
meets the curve at a glancing angle. Centring packs them half a port gap apart around the
middle, and on a round node may move an end that turns anyway to the free top or bottom border.

oneOf.description: Every end keeps the port the router spread it to.
Ellipse nodes centre their borders' ends.
Every node centres its borders' ends. Only ellipses move ends round a corner.

MergeEdges.description:
Which fan-outs and fan-ins [`Routing::merge_edges`] draws on a shared trunk.

A merge is made only where it adds no crossing or bend and cuts through no node.
[`crate::Layout::junctions`] marks the branch points.

oneOf.description: Every edge keeps its own port and line.
Edges leaving one node share a trunk.
Edges reaching one node share a trunk.
Both forks and joins.

OrderOptions.description:
Crossing-minimisation heuristic and group lane budgets.

How hard the ordering phases work is in [`OrderTuning`].

heuristic.description: Which one-sided heuristic the sweeps sort by. See [`OrderHeuristic`].

group_lane_budget_percent.description:
Crossings the lane pass may add to put each group ([`crate::Node::group`]) in a band of
its own, as a percentage of the crossings ordering left, plus
[`OrderTuning::group_lane_budget_floor`]. Default 0.

A banding that costs nothing is always taken. For clear lanes, try 100 here, a floor of 8
and [`OrderOptions::group_lane_area_percent`] of 50.

group_lane_area_percent.description:
How much wider the order axis may get, in percent, when the group bands are stacked into
disjoint slots. Default 0, which leaves the bands where the coordinate phases put them.

The stack is compressed to fit this budget, letting wide bands overlap at their edges.

group_lanes.description:
Whether group lanes are a preference traded against the two budgets above
([`GroupLanes::Soft`], the default) or required swimlanes ([`GroupLanes::Strict`]).

OrderHeuristic.description:
Which one-sided heuristic a crossing-minimisation sweep sorts a layer by. Default
[`OrderHeuristic::Alternate`].

Both place a node by where its neighbours in the previous layer sit. They differ on outliers:
Neighbours at `{0, 1, 20}` give position 7 under the barycentre and 1 under the median.

oneOf.description:
Weighted mean of the neighbours' positions (Sugiyama et al.). Heavy edges pull harder, so
the main flow ends up straighter.

Weighted median of the neighbours' positions (Eades and Wormald 1994), which has the
better worst-case guarantee on one bilayer.
Barycentre on even sweeps, median on odd ones. The best-scoring sweep is kept.

GroupLanes.description: How the groups ([`crate::Node::group`]) of a layered drawing are drawn.

oneOf.description:
Bands of the order axis where affordable. A banding over either
[`OrderOptions::group_lane_budget_percent`] or [`OrderOptions::group_lane_area_percent`]
is not drawn.

placement.description: Which optimiser places the order axis. Default [`Placement::NetworkSimplex`].

branch_bands.description:
Keep each branch off the main path in a band of its own, so one branch never slides into
a sibling's row. Default `true`. Graphs without a main path (several flows, caller seeds,
group lanes) are unaffected.

terminal_centering.description:
Centre a first- or last-layer terminal on the weighted median of its neighbours, so it
sits over its main flow. Default `false`, `true` in [`LayoutOptions::process_map`].

branch_style.description:
How a fork/join block's branches are drawn. See [`BranchStyle`]. Default
[`BranchStyle::Free`], but [`LayoutOptions::layered_default`] and
[`LayoutOptions::process_map`] use [`BranchStyle::StraightMain`].

CrossPlacement.description:
Which optimiser places the order axis.

Both keep the crossing-minimised order and every gap in [`crate::Spacing`]. They differ in
what they optimise within those constraints. [`CoordOptions`] defaults to
[`Placement::NetworkSimplex`].

oneOf.description:
Brandes-Kopf, as in dagre and ELK, followed by the straightness snap
([`CoordTuning::snap_rounds`]). Fast and local.

The dot placement (Gansner et al. 1993, section 4.2): A network simplex minimises the
total weighted cross-axis edge offset. Shorter edges and smaller area than Brandes-Kopf,
with more bends. Large graphs fall back to Brandes-Kopf
([`CoordTuning::simplex_max_nodes`]).

BranchStyle.description:
How the two branches of a fork/join block are drawn against each other.

[`crate::metrics::LayoutMetrics::split_alignment`] measures how many blocks come out aligned.

oneOf.description:
Keeps whatever placement produced. Suits graphs not read as blocks, such as dense
hub-and-spoke graphs.

One branch of each block runs straight from fork to join and the others are pushed aside
as skips. The straight branch is the heaviest, with ties going to the larger first node
along the layout axis.

The two branches sit at equal distance either side of the straight fork-join line. Only
possible when both branches start in the same layer. Adds crossings, so no preset uses it.

CompactionOptions.description: Cross-axis compaction. Its iteration counts are in [`CompactionTuning`].

mode.description: Whether the cross axis is compacted after placement.

Compaction.description: Whether the cross axis is compacted after placement. Default [`Compaction::None`].

oneOf.description: Leave the coordinates the placement passes produced.

Order-preserving priority compaction: Pack each layer, align it to its weighted-median
edges, then slide nodes toward their neighbours. Suits dense hub-and-spoke graphs.

SelfLoopOptions.description:
How self-loops (`source == target` edges) are drawn.

Self-loops take no part in cycle breaking, layering or ordering. Their room is reserved before
coordinate assignment, so placement widens exactly the slot the loops need.

side.description: Which border the loops bump out of. Default [`LoopSide::Auto`].

size.description:
How far the innermost loop reaches beyond the node's border. Default 15, the
[`Spacing::stub`] default, so a loop leaves its port by the same run as an ordinary edge.

gap.description:
Depth step between two loops stacked on one node, so `k` loops nest. Default 10, the
[`Spacing::self_loop_gap`] default.

label_gap.description: Clear space between the outer run of a loop and its own label box. Default 4.

LoopSide.description:
Which border of its node a self-loop bumps out of. Default [`LoopSide::Auto`].

The names are in flow terms, like [`crate::Margins`], so they hold for either [`Direction`].
`cross` is the order axis (along which one layer's nodes spread) and `along` the layer axis.

oneOf.description:
The positive order side (screen bottom in `LeftRight`, screen right in `TopBottom`). This
is the side [`crate::Margins::cross_pos`] reserves room on.
The negative order side.

The forward layer side, toward the next layer (screen right in `LeftRight`, screen bottom
in `TopBottom`).

Let the engine pick per node, once the layers are ordered.

A node with an order-axis neighbour on one side only uses the free side. Otherwise it uses
[`LoopSide::CrossPositive`], unless the node's own [`crate::Margins`] reserve more room on
the negative side.

LabelOptions.description: How edge labels are given room, and where in the drawing they end up.

reservation.description: When a layer gap is widened to hold a label.

placement.description: How the final position is chosen.

clearance.description:
Clear space a label tries to keep from node boxes, other labels and other edges. Soft: A
position with less clearance is penalised for the shortfall. Default 4.

LabelReservation.description:
When a layer gap is widened to hold the labels crossing it. Default
[`LabelReservation::WhenNeeded`].

Reservation is the only guarantee of room, and it costs width because every label widens its
gap.

oneOf.description: Every labelled edge widens its gap to hold its label.

Only a label too large for the order-axis space between two nodes of a layer
([`Spacing::node_gap`]) widens its gap. Smaller ones are left to
[`LabelPlacement::Candidates`], which can put them in that space. The test uses the label's
extent across the flow.

Nothing is reserved. Placement fits each label into whatever free space exists, and
takes the least-bad position when there is none.

LabelPlacement.description: How a label's final position is chosen. Default [`LabelPlacement::Candidates`].

oneOf.description: The middle of its reserved gap, with labels sharing a gap stacked across the flow.

The best of several positions along the edge's own polyline (near the source, middle or
target, on either side of the line), scored by what each one overlaps.

Effort.description:
How hard the engine works, as one dial over the iteration counts. Default
[`Effort::Balanced`].

`Balanced` leaves [`OrderTuning`] and [`CoordTuning`] as given, so hand-tuned counts survive.
Any other value overwrites the counts in its [`Effort::budget`]. `Thorough` usually saves a
few crossings on dense graphs for two to three times the time.

oneOf.description: Fewer restarts and sweeps, for interactive relayout of large graphs.
The [`Tuning`] counts as given.
More restarts and sweeps, for a final rendering.
Exactly these counts.

EffortBudget.description: The iteration counts one [`Effort`] resolves to.

exhaustive_layer_max.description: Brute-force permutation cap ([`OrderTuning::exhaustive_layer_max`]).

sifting_rounds.description: Sifting rounds per wide layer ([`OrderTuning::sifting_rounds`]).

pullin_rounds.description: Channel pull-in rounds, applied only when [`CoordTuning::pullin_rounds`] is non-zero.

kick_patience.description:
Rejected kicks per layer before the local search gives up on it
([`OrderTuning::kick_patience`]).

Limits.description:
Input size limits.

All `None` by default. Set them when the input is untrusted (e.g., JSON from a wasm caller).
Exceeding a limit is [`LayoutError::TooLarge`], never a hang or a panic.

max_dummies.description:
Largest accepted routing-waypoint count (one per layer a long edge passes), checked after
layering. [`crate::LayoutError::TooLarge`] names it `"routing waypoints"`.

WrapOptions.description:
Wrapping a long drawing into rows to fit a viewport shape. When a wrap pays is in
[`WrapTuning`].

viewport_aspect.description: Width over height of the viewport the drawing is shown in. Default `0`, never wrap.

strategy.description: Which edges of a cycle are drawn backwards.

CycleStrategy.description:
Which edges of a cyclic graph are drawn against the flow. Default
[`CycleStrategy::MinimumReversal`].

A layered drawing draws one edge per cycle backwards.

oneOf.description:
Reverse as little edge weight as possible (a heuristic minimum feedback arc set). Fewest
crossings, but a rare step can be drawn before the steps that lead to it.

Order the nodes inside a cycle by distance from where the flow enters it, so every
reversed edge reads as a return to an earlier point. Can cost crossings on dense graphs.

SeedMode.description:
How node positions given by the caller ([`crate::Node::position`]) steer a layout. Default
[`SeedMode::Placement`].

oneOf.description:
Seeds set the nodes' cross-axis positions, but layering and ordering run from scratch.
A changed graph can land in other layers and orders, so the drawing may jump.

Tuning.description:
Iteration counts, budgets and thresholds, tuned on the fixture corpus.

A non-`Balanced` [`LayoutOptions::effort`] overrides the ordering counts in [`OrderTuning`]
and [`CoordTuning::pullin_rounds`].

routing.description: The router's repair passes.

coords.description: The coordinate phases' rounds and budgets.

compaction.description: Priority compaction's rounds.

labels.description: Label placement's candidates and rounds.

wrap.description: When and how far a drawing is wrapped.

diagonal_clear.description:
Minimum clearance between a diagonal segment and a node box. A closer segment takes a
corner detour, since a graze reads as badly as a hit. Default 8.

diagonal_detour_margin.description: How far outside a node box a diagonal's corner detour is placed. Default 12.

bundle_nest_gap.description:
How far past the inner channel's turn an outer channel is carried when two nested
long-edge channels would otherwise cross at their shared target. Default 12.

endpoint_snap.description: Largest port jog that is straightened onto the edge's main track. Default 6.

endpoint_snap_min_track.description: Shortest segment that counts as a main track. Default 25.

step_flatten.description:
Tallest step (run, perpendicular jog, run) merged away after routing by moving one run onto
the other's line. Default `1.0e6` (no cap), `0.0` disables the pass.

A move is taken only if it hits no node box, keeps ports [`Spacing::port_gap`] apart, and
adds no crossing or overlap.

port_relax_clear.description:
Minimum distance between two ports on adjacent borders of one node, the corner case
`port_gap` does not cover. Default 10.

port_relax_step.description: Step of the greedy nudge that enforces `port_relax_clear`. Default 3.

port_relax_rounds.description: Iterations of that nudge per node. Default 48.

overlap_repair_rounds.description:
Rounds of the repair that separates two edges' runs drawn on one line along the layer
axis, where that adds no box hit or crossing. Default 8. `0` disables it.

overlap_repair_step.description:
How far that repair moves a run or a port, in one or two steps. Default 8. `0.0`
disables the repair.

OrderTuning.description:
How hard the crossing-minimisation and lane phases work ([`Tuning::order`]).

The counts do not scale with graph size. A non-`Balanced` [`Effort`] overwrites the restart,
sweep, permutation, sifting and kick counts.

seeds.description:
Ordering restarts. Default 9. The first three are structural (a DFS seed, its mirror, and
a DFS from the last layer), the rest deterministic shuffles of the first.

sweeps.description:
Upper bound on forward and backward sweeps per restart. Default 8. A restart stops early
after [`OrderTuning::sweep_stall`] sweeps without improvement.

sweep_stall.description:
Consecutive non-improving sweeps after which a restart gives up. Default 2. `0` is read as
`1`.

exhaustive_layer_max.description: Layers with 2 to this many nodes are ordered by trying every permutation. Default 5.

sifting_min_layer.description:
Layers wider than this get the sifting pass. Default 2. The kicks only visit layers that
sift, so raising it also removes layers from the local search.

sifting_rounds.description:
Upper bound on sifting rounds over the layer stack. Default 8. A round sifts every layer
still moving and wakes the neighbours of those that moved. It stops early when a round
moves nothing.

sifting_max_work.description:
Work ceiling for sifting one layer, in arc pairs (about `e^2` for `e` arcs on its two
sides). A heavier layer is left to the sweeps. Default 160000.

sifting_sweep_max_arcs.description:
Arc count up to which sifting also runs inside each restart's sweeps, instead of only on
the winning order. It multiplies sifting cost by the restart count. Default 20000.

kick_rounds.description:
Upper bound on kicks the iterated local search tries on the winning order. A kick reverses
a short run of one layer, re-sifts, and is kept only if strictly better. Usually
[`OrderTuning::kick_patience`] stops the pass first. Default 30000. `0` disables it.

kick_patience.description:
Consecutive rejected kicks per layer after which that layer leaves the kick pool. An
accepted kick resets its layer and both neighbours. Default 64. `0` is read as `1`.

kick_max_span.description:
Longest run of a layer one kick may reverse. Each kick picks a length from 2 up to this.
Default 8.

group_relax_iters.description:
Relaxation iterations that spread lane values from grouped to ungrouped nodes.
Default 64.

group_sort_rounds.description: Re-sort rounds of the group lane pass. Default 8.

group_lane_budget_floor.description:
Crossings the lane pass may add on top of [`OrderOptions::group_lane_budget_percent`].
Default 0. A nearly planar drawing has no crossings to take a percentage of, so this
floor is what lets it get lanes.

group_lane_sweeps.description:
Barycentre sweeps over the banded order, each re-sorting every layer within its bands.
Default 4.

group_lane_repair_rounds.description:
Rounds of band-preserving adjacent swaps that win back crossings the banding cost.
Default 3.

group_lane_order_rounds.description: Rounds of adjacent band swaps looking for a band order with fewer crossings. Default 2.

chain_lane_rounds.description:
Rounds of the chain-lane pass, which moves a long edge's waypoints past their neighbours
where that costs no crossing and lets the edge run on one lane. Default 3. `0` disables the
pass.

chain_lane_size_threshold.description:
On a graph with more routing waypoints than this, the chain-lane pass skips chains longer
than [`OrderTuning::chain_lane_max_span`]. Default 2000.

chain_lane_max_span.description: Longest chain the chain-lane pass still works on above the size threshold. Default 12.

chain_lane_max_steps.description:
How many positions the chain-lane pass may move one waypoint in one go. A walk is kept
whole if it opens the lane, else undone. Default 5.

balance_rounds.description:
Rounds of the side-balancing pass, which mirrors branches off the main path to whichever
side evens out the layers, where that costs no crossing. Default 4. `0` disables it.

CoordTuning.description: Iteration counts and budgets of the coordinate phases ([`Tuning::coords`]).

simplex_max_nodes.description:
Auxiliary-graph size (layered nodes plus arcs) above which [`Placement::NetworkSimplex`]
falls back to Brandes-Kopf. Default 10000.

simplex_max_pivots.description:
Simplex iterations before [`Placement::NetworkSimplex`] stops with its best placement so
far. Every iteration is feasible, so a capped solve is still a valid drawing. Default
50000.

simplex_face_rounds.description:
Rounds of the walk over the simplex's optimal face that re-places each long edge, heaviest
first, on the fewest lanes possible at the same cost. Default 2. `0` switches it off.
Brandes-Kopf ignores it.

snap_rounds.description:
Rounds of the straightness snap after Brandes-Kopf. Default 8. The network simplex
ignores it.

main_path_room.description:
How much wider, in percent, the drawing may get to draw its heaviest source-to-sink path
as one straight line, but at least the widest node on the path. Default 15. `0` turns the
pass off.

balance_width_slack.description:
How much wider than the balanced placement one of Brandes-Kopf's four biased passes may
be and still be chosen, in percent. Default 20.

flatten_room.description:
Pixels of layer width one removed staircase step is worth when chain flattening pushes a
node aside to free a lane. Default 300. `0` turns the phase off.

pullin_rounds.description:
Rounds of channel pull-in, which moves a long edge's waypoints past a real node standing
between them and their endpoints' line when crossings allow. Default 0 (off), 3 in
[`LayoutOptions::process_map`].

branch_rounds.description:
Rounds of the [`BranchStyle`] pass. Each round walks every block innermost-first and
stops early once a round aligns nothing new. Default 3.

offset_rounds.description: Rounds of rigid per-layer offsetting. Default 24.

refine_rounds.description: Rounds of per-node refinement inside the packed envelope. Default 8.

LabelTuning.description: The candidate positions and rounds of label placement ([`Tuning::labels`]).

fractions.description:
Fractions along its own polyline at which a label is tried, besides the midpoint of the
longest segment. Ties go to the earlier fraction. Default `[0.5, 0.32, 0.68, 0.18, 0.82]`.

side_steps.description:
How far off its line a label may be pushed, as multiples of the distance that just clears
the line (half the label's extent across the line, plus the stroke, plus
[`LabelOptions::clearance`]). Both sides are tried, nearest first. Default `[1, 2, 4, 8]`.

rounds.description:
Rounds of placement. Round one ignores other labels, and each further round re-places
every label against the others. Default 2. `0` places nothing.

WrapTuning.description:
When and how far a drawing is wrapped once [`WrapOptions::viewport_aspect`] asks for it
([`Tuning::wrap`]).

max_rows.description: Most rows a drawing is wrapped into. Default 4.

min_gain.description:
Scale factor by which the drawing must grow in the viewport for a wrap to be taken.
Default 1.2. Every edge across a cut gets a U-turn, which a small gain does not pay for.

max_cut_edges.description: Most edges one cut may carry to the next row. Default 4.

OCDeclareLabels.description: How an arc shows its object types.

oneOf.description: A chip naming the types, e.g., `Each(orders), Any(items)`.
Discs on the line: one for each, three for all, one filled and two hollow for any.

ObjectInvolvementCounts.description: Stores statistics on the number of objects of a certain type involved with an activity or in an O2O relationship.

min.description: The minimum number of objects of a given type involved in a single instance.

max.description: The maximum number of objects of a given type involved in a single instance.

args.title: OCDeclareStyle
args.description: Colors and sizes of an OC-DECLARE drawing.

base.description: Colors and paddings shared with every other model.

plain_activities.description: Draw the activities in the base node colors instead of tinting each one.

fill_lightness.description: How far towards white an activity's color is washed for its fill.

marker.description: Color of the markers, and of an arc that names no object type.

BaseStyle.description: Colors, sizes and paddings shared by all model drawings.

background.description: Page background. `None` leaves the SVG transparent.

padding.description: Space kept around the drawing's bounding box, in px.

corner_radius.description: Corner radius of a box-shaped node.

args.title: StyleOverrides
args.description:
Per-element style changes, keyed by the index of the node or edge in the model's graph, which
is also its index in the layout and in the layout request's `nodes` and `edges`.

nodes.description: By node index.

edges.description: By edge index.
